#927. Were any current Man City players signed during charges period?

Manchester City captain Ruben Dias has made more than 250 club appearances since his arrival in 2020

No member of Manchester City's current squad was signed during the period in which an independent commission found the club guilty of all charges relating to breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations.

Those offences all came between 2009 and 2018. City have denied any wrongdoing and appealed against all of the charges against them.

The club's longest-serving first-team player who was purchased from another club is Portuguese centre-back and club captain Ruben Dias, who joined from Benfica in 2020.

Norway striker Erling Haaland is the next longest-serving arrival, joining from Borussia Dortmund in the summer of 2022.

Midfielder Phil Foden is the only player to have played for the club during the period in which they breached the league's financial rules, but was not a senior signing having come through the club's youth ranks.

Foden, 26, made his first-team debut in a Champions League match against Feyenoord in November 2017.

Like Foden, versatile midfielder Rico Lewis is also a product of the club's academy but did not make his senior debut until August 2022.

All of the club's other senior players were signed between 2023 and 2026.

#926. Meet the youngest top-flight manager in Europe

Jordan Hadaway has been in charge of Llandudno since August 2023; at 18, he was managing Caerwys and a 41-year-old captain; now 25, he has a UEFA A Licence and took the Seasiders back to the Cymru Premier with promotion in 2025/26

Football Journalist @DanLong__

As football has evolved, so have routes into football management.

Once almost exclusively the preserve of former professionals, a playing career is no longer a prerequisite.

That has opened the door to the younger generation. Thirteen managers and head coaches in England's top four divisions are under 40, with Brighton's Fabian Hurzeler the youngest at 33.

But the Cymru Premier - formerly known as the Welsh Premier League - is home to the youngest top-flight manager in Europe.

Last season, Jordan Hadaway guided Llandudno to promotion from the Cymru North. In July, he turned the grand old age of 25.

Hadaway already had the presence of mind to focus on coaching, rather than playing, by 14.

He completed his Level 1 Leaders Award two days after his 16th birthday and was working towards his UEFA B Licence by 18, when he was in charge at Caerwys and working with a 41-year-old captain.

Later, he coached for the Real Madrid Foundation and, in 2024, he passed his A Licence. He counts Nigel Adkins and Robert Earnshaw among those to have helped him along the way.

During his time at Caerwys, Hadaway wrote to Roy Hodgson, who was then in charge of Crystal Palace.

"He was the oldest manager in league football and I was the youngest manager in football, so my college tutor said to me 'Why don't you just write to him?'" he tells Sky Sports.

"I got an email from his personal assistant and he invited me in, but the day I was due to go down, Covid happened. By the time everything opened back up, he had been sacked!

"It was a bit of a nightmare because I really wanted to go and meet him, but I guess things happen for a reason, don't they?"

It is clear his strong work ethic has helped him progress.

"While I was studying at Liverpool Hope University, some days I'd be up at 2.30am or 3am going to work in the bakery for a family friend as they'd lost staff because of Covid," he says.

"I'd stay there until 9.30am, go to a lecture from 11am until 2pm and then I'd coach from maybe 4pm until 9pm. It was a full-on period in my life!"

And it has not slowed down, given he now balances his part-time managerial role with a full-time role as a teacher.

In December 2022, Hadaway left his role as assistant manager at Cefn Druids to become Llandudno U19s manager, as well as the club's head of youth development.

By the start of the 2023/24 season, he had been named interim first-team manager of a club whos squad and staff had been decimated after its artificial playing surface was condemned by the Welsh FA.

"Everyone had walked away and we were two weeks away from starting the season," he recalls.

"The chairman said to me: 'Will you just try and keep us in the league and make sure we have a club? I don't care if we get relegated if that's what has to happen as long as we've got a team and a club at the end of it.'

"Everyone around me, I'll be honest, told me don't take it. My mum even says to me today: 'I can't believe you took that job'.

"But I saw it as an opportunity to go and try and prove people wrong at a very big club in Wales that has an amazing facility and a good fanbase.

"I had the smallest budget in the league by a country mile. I had one player two weeks before the start of the season and no management team. I had to put all that together in two weeks. We were favourites to get relegated, but I never once thought we would.

"We managed to finish 12th out of 16 and we got to a cup final that year. It's quite incredible, really."

Two years later, he took the club one step further.

"My aim was always to be a Welsh Premier League manager by the time I was 27, 28. Did I ever think I was going to get there? No. It's amazing.

"I'm lucky I've had very good players and very good staff that have enabled me to push the club to that standard. It's not all about me, it's about everybody involved.

"I got quite emotional on that afternoon we got promoted. It was an achievement that probably will stick with me and be one of my best forever."

Asked if he has aged beyond his years with the way his career has progressed, Hadaway quips: "Yes - I think my hairline's shown that!

"A lot of people say I'm the oldest 25-year-old they've ever met. I think I am mature, but I'm mature because of the people I've grown up around. The people you spend the most time with have the biggest impact on you."

That maturity is reflected in his attitude towards what comes next.

Many would leap to the conclusion that, if he is doing well at 25 in Wales, a career over the border in England will be on the cards soon.

That may well come to be true, but Hadaway is in no immediate rush.

"Don't get me wrong, I would love to do it [work in the Premier League or EFL]," he adds.

"However, I love my job and I love supporting young people that need the support in school, and I think it would have to be a very good opportunity to take me away from what I'm doing currently. I'm also not naive.

"But I don't think I should get given a chance because I'm the youngest manager in top-flight football - I think I should be given a chance because I'm good enough.

"If we had this interview again in 10 years' time and I was still at Llandudno, I would be happy, because I'm not someone that chases the stars. I'm someone that likes to make sure I'm doing a good job where I'm at and make sure that when I leave, I've left it in a very good place and it's stable."

For someone who has accomplished so much so young, perhaps Hadaway's strength is in knowing there is no need to rush.

#925. Who is close to a yellow card suspension in Champions League?

Arsenal forward Kai Havertz is among the players to have received two yellow cards in this season's Champions League

Players will receive a one-match ban should they receive four yellow cards before the semi-finals of the Champions League.

This rule runs from the start of the league phase until the end of the quarter-finals. After then, all yellow cards are wiped out and players cannot be suspended for multiple yellow cards.

Yellow cards that result in a red card during a match do not count towards a player's tally, as a separate suspension will be served.

The same rules apply for both the Europa League and the Conference League.

During the opening three rounds of the Champions League, 16 players received two yellow cards, meaning they are now two cautions away from a one-match ban.

Shakhtar Donetsk's Marlon Gomes, Villarreal's Santiago Mourino and Inter Milan's Hakan Calhanoglu are each on three yellow cards, putting them on the brink of a ban.

Players can also be suspended if they pick up six, eight or 10 yellow cards. This would also result in a one-match suspension every time a player hits an even number of yellow cards above four.

Red cards result in a one-match suspension, with Bayern Munich's Michael Olise missing his side's earlier clash with Arsenal after being sent off against Viking in the previous round of fixtures.

Uefa may increase the length of a red card ban for serious offences such as violent conduct.

*denotes two yellows that resulted in a red card

The following players will miss the next round of league phase matches following either a yellow or red card suspension:

#924. CF Montreal are for sale: What it means, how much it could cost, and what’s next for the MLS club

In an emotional press conference, CF Montreal’s founder and owner Joey Saputo refused to rule out relocation

In a rare press conference, CF Montreal owner Joey Saputo announced that his family was beginning the process of “initiating a structured sale process” of the MLS club. Saputo informed the public of his intentions on Monday afternoon, pausing multiple times to fight back tears after over three decades of owning the Quebecois club.

“This decision is neither driven by urgency, nor dictated by circumstance,” Saputo said in his initial scripted remarks. “It’s the result of a careful and deliberate reflection on where we stand today, and more importantly, on the opportunities that lie ahead for the club.”

Throughout his statement, Saputo stressed his desire to keep the club in Montreal, saying he hoped to find someone who “shares commitment to Montreal and who will ensure that the club remains in the city for many years to come.”

Yet, more than half an hour into the event after the floor was open for in-person questions, Saputo refused to rule out selling to a buyer who might move the club.

“I will not discount the club to the point of just giving it away just for the sake of giving it away,” Saputo said. “I want to be perfectly clear. I love this club. I will love this club to stay here. But if an owner comes in that doesn’t have the capacity to keep the club at the level that it needs to be at, and to spend the money that needs to be spent in order to bring in the players that this city wants to see, then at that point I’m not doing anyone a favor by selling it to someone just to keep it here.

“As much as I would love for this club to be here, if someone has the capacity to do it, and I feel that they have the capacity to do it, then I would love for this club to be here, and continue to build on what we did. But if there isn’t, and there’s an offer that comes in to relocate the club, and it’s in line with Major League Soccer and what they want to, then yeah, that’s where it’s going to be.”

Saputo declined to provide estimates for his selling point, nor for his and MLS’s timeline to find a suitable buyer. Saputo said the sales process will be conducted in coordination with MLS as well as the club’s retained investment bankers.

But based on recent history, Saputo stands to receive many times more than the $40m expansion fee he paid to join the league in 2012.

In January, the Illig family sold 71% of ownership of Sporting Kansas City to Peter Malouk at a $700m valuation. In May, the Haslem family sold a 37% stake in the Columbus Crew at a valuation of $900m. Both teams own their own home stadium; Forbes rated SKC as the league’s 16th most valuable franchise in 2025, while Columbus ranked 18th at the time of their partial sale.

As of June 2025, Forbes ranked CF Montréal as the second least-valuable club in MLS at an estimation of $435m, only ahead of Stan Kroenke’s Colorado Rapids. The club does own its own stadium, Stade Saputo – modestly sized at just over 19,000 capacity but on its day one of the better atmospheres in the league.

However, MLS’s decision to flip its season calendar means that Montreal could be in line to play more matches in the winter – a tough proposition in Stade Saputo’s outdoor environs. The Montreal Olympic Stadium, located next door, is due for a modernization and will reopen in 2028 but the club would be tenants there, should they move on a more permanent basis.

Saputo initially launched the club in late 1992, then as the Montreal Impact, serving as the club’s day-to-day steward for most of his ownership tenure. He guided the club through two decades in five different leagues before becoming an MLS expansion franchise, debuting in 2012. Two years later, Saputo led a consortium that bought a controlling interest in Italian Serie A side Bologna, where he remains president.

Saputo acknowledged an earlier aspiration, stated in early 2023, to position Montreal for long-term success on and off the field. That declaration came after the club had lost Wilfried Nancy to the Columbus Crew after two seasons of greatly outperforming expectations under the French manager. Nancy went on to win MLS Cup that season and reached the Concacaf Champions League final in 2024 with the Crew.

Jonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer.

Meanwhile, Montreal have been at the very bottom of MLS since Nancy’s departure. Only three other teams have accrued as few points (139) over the past four seasons: DC United (139), Sporting KC (136), and Toronto FC (130). Montréal has won just one playoff game since 2016, with their best stretches directly coinciding with the brief tenures of striker Didier Drogba (from 2015 to 2016) and Nancy on the touchline (from 2021 to 2022).

Montreal have routinely been among MLS’s most thrifty operations this decade in terms of roster spending, both on salaries and transfer fees. Saputo acknowledged the need for the next owner to “start spending in line with some of the other teams,” a tacit admission of missing that mark.

“We’re going to continue to run the club,” Saputo said regarding the interim. “It will be challenging for us, but we are going to stay here until we find the buyer for the club.”

According to Saputo, yes. In opening that door, the club becomes the second of MLS’s three Canadian teams to be relocation candidates – the other being the Vancouver Whitecaps, who have been in the midst of their own sale and facilities quagmire.

These days, when an American sports league is looking to move a team, Las Vegas is an obvious first suitor. The city is no longer just for gambling and debauchery, with the NHL’s Vegas Golden Knights joining as an expansion side in 2017. The NFL’s Raiders became the first team to relocate to Nevada in 2020, leaving Oakland. The WNBA relocated the San Antonio Stars, now the Las Vegas Aces, in 2022.

Golden Knights owner Bill Foley initially looked into buying an MLS franchise to play in the city, only to ultimately buy AFC Bournemouth for £100m (roughly $121m at the time).

“MLS, unfortunately, requires a stadium to be built and, in the United States, that is costing $600-700m,” Foley said in 2022. “The franchise fee itself, I think, is $300m so you are into it for a billion dollars before you have a team. I thought Bournemouth was a bargain.”

Sacramento is another popular suggestion for relocation. The California capital was awarded an MLS expansion slot in 2019, but primary owner Ron Burkle put those plans on “indefinite hiatus” two years later citing financial strain due to the Covid-19 pandemic. MLS ultimately rescinded their claim as the ownership group folded, and awarded its 30th expansion slot to San Diego. The city’s second-division team, Sacramento Republic, is currently constructing a 20,000-seat venue to open in 2028 on the site which was previously intended to house Burkle’s MLS team.

Other cities that have confirmed interest in MLS, either at the government level or from local buyers, include Phoenix, Indianapolis, and Detroit.

Saputo’s stressing that local buyers won’t be given a discounted rate to keep the club in Quebec evokes memories of another longtime Montreal sporting organization. In the early 2000s, the MLB’s Montreal Expos struggled to find a buyer who could afford to keep the team in the city while meeting the requisite and rapidly growing financial might.

The Expos played their final season in 2004, relocating to the US capital and playing as the Washington Nationals for the ensuing 22 years to date.

#923. Why England called up Jobe Bellingham ahead of Cole Palmer or Phil Foden - both players of a bygone era

England have called up Jobe Bellingham - and the data says it makes perfect sense

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Jobe Bellingham's England call-up isn't the first to come under scrutiny, and it certainly won't be the last.

But it is somewhat cruel that the midfielder's first-ever international appearance looks to be met with weary suspicion that it's down to connections rather than what he can actually do on the pitch.

Because the truth is, England could actually do with Jobe Bellingham – despite the embarrassment of riches that the Three Lions have in that area of the pitch.

Thomas Tuchel has Jude Bellingham as his first-choice No.10. Beyond that, Morgan Rogers, Morgan Gibbs-White, Eberechi Eze, Cole Palmer and Phil Foden have all competed for that position over the past 18 months.

Each of them offers something a little different to Bellingham: Eze and Palmer, for example, have the deftness of pass, while Foden and Rogers are capable of arriving at the edge of the box for a finesse finish into the bottom corner.

But Jobe is a stylistic replacement for Jude, and the data backs it up: looking at stats courtesy of Gradient Sports, Bellingham the younger ranks third out of our seven candidates for open play shooting – which measures a player's individual execution and decision-making quality relative to expectation – behind Jude and Morgan Rogers.

Jobe is fourth for pressured passes, too, with Jude in second, as they've both picked up a similar level of press resistance from those years of development in the Bundesliga. But it's defensively that they're most similar.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

Jude is in the 95th percentile for duel-winning across Europe, with Jobe in the 77th. The Bellingham brothers top our prospective magnificent seven, with Eze lagging behind in third – and in 1v1 defending, Jude again leads, with Jobe in second.

Across the board, Rogers is still the closest to Jude Bellingham in terms of all-round game. When it comes to tackle resistance, Jude leads the group with a score of 92.6 on the scale, but Rogers is the next closest at 82.6. By comparison, Jobe is at 76.1, and players like Eze (64.4) and Palmer (70.6) fall far behind. Rogers is also the clear runner-up in both On-Ball Attacking (78.6) and Open Play (75.1) categories, with Jobe scoring much lower here (65.7 and 69.6, respectively).

While Jobe lacks Jude’s elite attacking output and ball retention, he manages to match Jude's defensive and out-of-possession numbers reasonably well. Incidentally, fellow first-time call-up Josh King ranks well for both duels and ball-carrying – finding himself even ahead of Jude.

The Bellingham brothers' continued rise and the inclusion of talents like Gibbs-White and King point to a change in tack from manager Thomas Tuchel. Both Phil Foden and Cole Palmer have enjoyed clamour from fans for them to both start for England in the past – but the German resisted taking either to the World Cup.

And digging into the data, both of them represent hugely different profiles to their contemporaries. Palmer offers elite passing and carrying, actually beating Jude in Ball Carrying (79.5 vs Jude's 67.6) and Through Balls (83.7 vs Jude's 77.8). However, he is a poor stylistic replacement for Jude in physical midfield battles, scoring the lowest of the group in All Duels (53.7 vs Jude's 76.0). Foden rates significantly lower than Jude in physical areas like Tackle Resistance (71.5) and 1v1 Defending (64.4), too, perhaps indicating why he's seldom been used centrally for his country.

They're both elite players on their day: more technical and pass-heavy, but less robust in physical duels – and including players for their technical prowess while ignoring defensive limitations seems to be something of the past now, even at international level. A move towards Spain-like schemers that began with the Elite Player Performance Plan in 2012 really is old news now and this confirms it.

#922. Which game will Chelsea's Palmer miss after red card?

Cole Palmer was sent off in the second half of Chelsea's 2-0 loss at Stamford Bridge

Chelsea's Cole Palmer will not miss the Blues' Premier League meeting with Manchester United on Saturday, despite being sent off in his side's last Premier League match.

Palmer was shown two yellow cards in the second half of the Blues' defeat by rivals Tottenham Hotspur on Saturday. That dismissal meant that Palmer was handed a one-match ban.

The England playmaker was shown his first caution for an off-the-ball incident involving Spurs' Mateus Fernandes. He was then shown a second yellow card for a foul on Conor Gallagher.

In most cases, this would be served in that team's next Premier League match. However, Palmer will not miss Chelsea's meeting with United at Stamford Bridge.

Instead, Palmer will be banned for the Blues' EFL Cup fourth-round match away at Liverpool on Wednesday night.

This is because red card suspensions are carried out across domestic competitions rather than being specific to the competition they were received in.

Suspensions for an accumulation of yellow cards across a campaign are served in the competition in which they are received.

So while the Blues will miss Palmer for their trip to Anfield, he will be available to face United three days after the club's cup tie on Merseyside.

#920. Which Premier League players are set for yellow card suspensions?

Harry Maguire and Alexis Mac Allister are among 13 players on the brink of a one-match ban

The first one-match suspensions for yellow card offences in the 2026-27 Premier League season have now been served.

Hull City's Matt Crooks and Aston Villa's Matty Cash became the first players to receive a ban for accumulating five yellow cards before gameweek 19.

Players receive a one-match suspension if they pick up five or more yellow cards prior to the conclusion of their team's 19th league match of the season.

There are now 13 players sitting on four bookings after 10 rounds of matches, meaning they must avoid another yellow card prior to the halfway point of the season to avoid a ban.

Bournemouth have the most players on the brink of a ban, with three players one yellow card away from suspension.

After that date, the threshold increases to 10 yellow cards. Any player reaching that number before the end of their club's 32nd league match of the season will receive a two-match suspension.

From that point, there are further thresholds at 15 and 20 yellow cards.

For players reaching 15 cautions, they incur a three-match suspension. Punishments for players reaching 20 yellow cards are determined by a regulatory commission.

Those cut-offs do not reset until the end of the Premier League season.

In the Championship, League One and League Two, there are similar thresholds.

However, with those three divisions having 46 rounds of league matches instead of 38, players have to avoid getting 10 yellow cards before the end of the 37th league match in order to not receive a two-match suspension.

In those divisions, the yellow cards are reset at the end of the league season and do not include matches in the play-offs.

The following players have served a one-match ban and will now receive a two-match ban if they reach ten bookings before game week 32:

Matt Crooks - Hull City (five yellow cards)

If any of the following players receive another Premier League yellow card before the season's halfway point, they will be banned for one match:

Pascal Gross - Brighton & Hove Albion (four)

Oliver Boscagli - Brighton & Hove Albion (four)

The following players will miss their club's next set of fixtures:

Max Dowman - Arsenal (red card suspension)

Jean-Philippe Mateta - Crystal Palace (red card suspension)

Igor Thiago - Brentford (red card suspension)

#919. Cheltenham Festival-winning jockey O'Brien dies

Two-time Cheltenham Festival-winning jockey Tom O'Brien has passed away at the age of 39 following a lengthy battle with cancer; As a rider, O'Brien notched five Grade One successes before retiring in 2023.

Multiple Grade One-winning jockey Tom O’Brien has died at the age of 39.

O'Brien, who retired from the saddle in April 2023, rose to prominence with trainers Peter Bowen and Philip Hobbs and enjoyed a breakthrough season in 2006/07 with over 100 winners in that campaign.

The first of five Grade One successes came aboard Souffleur for Bowen in the 2007 Challow Novices' Hurdle, while later in his career O'Brien would strike up a memorable partnership with Hobbs' fan favourite Thyme Hill, landing the 2021 Liverpool Hurdle and 2022 Kauto Star Novices' Chase.

O'Brien also rode Dream Alliance to his against-all-odds victory in the 2009 Welsh Grand National, a story which would inspire a Hollywood film called Dream Horse.

Reflecting on O'Brien's life, Philip Hobbs said: "He came to our yard from Ireland having not ridden in a race, but it soon became obvious he was pretty talented and he was with us from the start of his career until the end.

"He was in the shadow of Richard Johnson for a long time being second jockey and then became first jockey after Richard retired, which went well. His biggest win was Thyme Hill in the Grade One at Aintree and he was always very reliable and a very good bloke.

"There's lots of good memories and there were lots of winners and I'd kept in touch with Tom since his retirement as he only lived half an hour away - he was only in our yard about three weeks ago.

"It's very sad, particularly for his wife Hayley and two young children."

Speaking on the Nick Luck Daily Podcast, Johnson White - now co-trainer with Philip Hobbs, said: "You couldn't get a harder working, nicer family man. I messaged Richard Johnson this morning and he sent a message back saying 'life is so cruel' and realistically you can't say any more than that. He leaves a lovely wife Hayley, two wonderful boys and a loving family that were there with him until the end."

Writing on Instagram, weighing room colleague Harry Cobden posted: "Gutted to hear the news about Tom. He was a great friend and a brilliant jockey. He will be hugely missed by everyone who knew him. Thoughts are with Hayley, Archie and Toby, and all his family and friends."

British Horseracing Authority (BHA) Chief Executive Brant Dunshea paid tribute, saying: "Tom was held in the highest esteem and meant so much to so many people across our sport, who benefitted from his kindness and loyal friendship.

"He touched countless lives on both sides of the Irish Sea, bringing joy to everyone who had the privilege of knowing him and watching what he did best, on and off the racecourse.

"He will be hugely missed and his loss is immensely difficult to process. The racing family is distraught, but I know how we will all rally round to provide each other with support, comfort and to remember Tom as we knew him best: a brilliant jockey, a valued colleague, a loyal friend and above all a loving husband and devoted father."

Trainer Christian Williams posted on X: "Kind, talented, humble and a true gentleman. Tom was a joy to be around and a privilege to have in the saddle. A friend to so many and of course, always smiling. Our thoughts and prayers are with Hayley, Archie, Toby, their families and many, many friends."

Writing on X, Sky Sports Racing broadcaster Mike Cattermole said: "Really saddened to hear about the passing of Tom O'Brien at 39. Obviously an excellent jockey but just a lovely guy, so gentle and humble. Thinking about all those who were close to him. Life is such a lottery."

#917. Why your physics project needs an anthropologist

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Jaco de Swart is a historian and anthropologist of science at the University of Cambridge, UK.

The TAMBO team assesses suitable observatory sites in the Andes Mountains of Peru.Credit: Jaco de Swart

It is uncommon for a social scientist to have a seat at a meeting about an astronomical observatory, let alone for them to jointly lead one. For one-quarter of attendees to be social-science scholars is almost unprecedented. But that’s exactly what happens at meetings about the Tau Air-shower Mountain-based Observatory (TAMBO), a proposed detector to be built in the Peruvian Andes to look for cosmic particles called tau neutrinos.

Space diplomacy: bridging the operating gaps between myriad missions

Space diplomacy: bridging the operating gaps between myriad missions

Tau neutrinos are elusive fundamental particles that are transmitted through space from black holes and other distant sources. When these particles interact with rocks on Earth, they can produce a shower of other, short-lived particles. The idea behind TAMBO is that if such a shower were emitted from one side of a deep canyon, it could be picked up by an array of 5,000 detectors on the other side (TAMBO collaboration. Nature Astron. 10, 947–951; 2026). The Andes Mountains of Peru contain many promising sites.

For those who live in the area, however, the case for TAMBO is less clear. The Andes are a sensitive ecological environment and home to Indigenous farming communities that consider the mountains sentient beings that are integral to their society. The area is also affected by legal and illegal mining, large-scale infrastructure projects and legacies of colonialism. This all leads to scepticism towards large projects that are developed by people from outside the area.

I am the co-principal investigator of the TAMBO collaboration, alongside Peruvian neutrino physicist Carlos Argüelles at Harvard University in Cambridge, Massachusetts. I lead the social-science and ‘responsible siting’ side of the project. Having received funding to build a proof-of-principle experiment called TAMBITO, we are searching for a potential location for the observatory.

Developing astronomers in Africa: ‘We wanted to create a discipline’

Developing astronomers in Africa: ‘We wanted to create a discipline’

Since 2024, the TAMBO collaboration has built partnerships with 11 Peruvian institutions, which are involved in the design and development of the telescope. Scientific links are an important starting point, but they are not enough. No matter what their discovery potential is, big scientific experiments are not beneficial to everyone. For example, construction of the Thirty Meter Telescope has been stalled since 2015 because of protests triggered by objections to its planned site on Maunakea in Hawaii — a mountain that is sacred in Native Hawaiian culture.

To integrate environmental care into the project and build good relationships with the communities that might host the telescope, TAMBO brought in experts on the Andean region. In 2024, the collaboration held a workshop at Harvard’s Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study, at which scholars and policymakers discussed what equitable astrophysics in Peru would look like. This led to the formation of a responsible-siting team that includes geographers, sociologists and anthropologists who have worked in the Andes.

#916. Felix Nmecha denies goal celebrations promote ‘intolerance, discrimination and hate’

Celebrations linked to ultra-conservative Christian group

‘Our message is of love’ Nmecha says in reply to criticism

The Borussia Dortmund and Germany midfielder Felix Nmecha has responded to criticism of goal celebrations linked to an evangelical network by saying they have been misunderstood and are not meant to promote “intolerance, discrimination, or hate in any form”.

Nmecha, a devout Christian, was criticised by the Dortmund official supporters’ group at the weekend for celebrating goals with a gesture signifying the “The King’s Return” campaign linked to Ballers in God (BIG), a network of Christian football players. The German public broadcaster ARD has linked BIG to ultra-conservative positions on issues including homosexuality and transgender identity.

“My celebration is not intended to promote myself or any organisation,” Nmecha wrote in a social media post on Tuesday. “Rather, it is about laying my ‘crown’ before the soon coming King and pointing to Jesus, my hope and strength. My message has never been about promoting intolerance, discrimination, or hate in any form.

“As Christians, our message is one of love and respect for everyone, regardless of where they come from, what they believe, or what their worldview may be.”

In a statement, Dortmund official supporters’ group said: “We oppose religious networks that, under the guise of faith, propagate a worldview in which individuals are denigrated or excluded based on their sexual orientation, gender identity, way of life, or personal choices”.

Dortmund said on Sunday that it understood the fans’ concerns and would speak to Nmecha. “For Borussia Dortmund, it is essential to take the concerns and needs of the fanbase seriously and to address them,” read a statement. “Naturally, we also take the current media coverage and the associated questions and discussions very seriously.”

The news agency DPA reported that Jürgen Klopp, Germany’s head coach, has already spoken to Nmecha about the issue at the national team camp in Herzogenaurach, Bavaria, before the upcoming Nations League games.

#915. Super League clubs vote to expand to 15 teams

Super League clubs have voted to expand competition to 15 teams for the 2027 season; Championship side London Broncos are favourites for inclusion; the league also voted in favour of two salary cap amendments that allow clubs more flexibility with young players and injuries

The Super League has announced that its 14 clubs have voted in favour of a motion to expand to 15 teams for the 2027 season.

"Super League (Europe) Ltd has today held a shareholders' meeting to determine how many clubs will take part in the competition in 2027," a statement from the league read.

"Having agreed in favour of moving from 14 to 15 clubs, SLE has passed their decision on to the Rugby Football League Board.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

"The RFL Board will now set out criteria and assemble a panel to run the process to judge against it.

"A recommendation will be made in due course."

It is understood that clubs will now be invited to apply to be the 15th team in the competition.

London Broncos, who have made no secret of their desire to be in the top flight, completed the treble in 2026 during a brilliant season for them in the Championship.They are expected to apply to be the next club in Super league. It is not yet known if any other clubs will join the process.After London went back down to the Championship, they were took over by an ownership group including NRL and Brisbane Broncos legend Darren Lockyer.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Clubs also voted in favour of two amendments to the league's salary cap regulations that allow clubs more flexibility with young players and injuries.

The first allows teams to claim salary cap dispensation if a player is injured for over eight cap-relevant matches, allowing clubs to sign a replacement player for the period.

It also forbids teams from claiming further salary cap dispensation should a player who was already exempt from salary cap implications becomes re-injured later in the season, unless he missed a further eight matches which affect the salary cap.

The second allows teams to feature a young player aged 23 and under - who has not previously played in any salary capped games - in two matches without triggering an increase in a club's salary cap spending, with that figure increasing to 50% should they play between three and five matches.

Should the player feature in more than five matches, the full amount of their salary will be applied to the cap.

#914. Rui Pinto’s lawyers in talks with UK authorities over deal for Manchester City whistleblower

He is willing to assist in exchange for protection

Rui Pinto’s lawyers are in talks with British authorities over a potential cooperation agreement under which the Manchester City whistleblower could help to expose serious financial and sporting crime in the UK.

According to information obtained by the Guardian, the Serious Fraud Office has contacted Pinto after it emerged he was willing to assist British authorities with their investigations in exchange for protection.

William Bourdon, Pinto’s lawyer, who has represented whistleblowers such as Edward Snowden and Julian Assange, told the Guardian that contact had been established. “I can confirm that the process is under way,” he said, without providing further details.

If an agreement is reached, the Football Leaks founder could become a significant source of information in investigations into financial crime involving football, law firms and powerful business figures. Between 2015 and 2019, Pinto collected tens of millions of files containing sensitive information. He may be able to assist the SFO in identifying potential tax offences and other irregularities that would otherwise have gone undetected.

The development comes at a significant moment for the 38-year-old Pinto, with his future under Portugal’s witness protection programme uncertain.

Pinto rose to prominence by exposing some of the football industry’s most closely guarded secrets. These included Cristiano Ronaldo’s tax affairs, plans by Europe’s leading clubs to establish a breakaway European Super League and a series of controversial financial arrangements. His revelations triggered investigations and contributed to legal proceedings involving clubs and players across several countries.

More recently, documents collected and leaked by the whistleblower became relevant to the Premier League’s investigation into Manchester City, which resulted in the club being found in breach of financial rules.

The information gathered by Pinto is in the possession of French authorities, who sought previously to include him in a witness protection programme. His arrest by Portuguese police in Hungary in January 2019 disrupted those plans, although France has maintained contact with him. Between his arrest in Hungary and his extradition to Portugal, French authorities travelled to Budapest and copied the contents of the electronic devices in his possession.

Pinto was informed on 30 September, just as his name had made headlines again after the City ruling, that he would no longer be protected by the Portuguese authorities after six years under the witness protection programme. Although the authorities maintained there was no threat to his life, he was advised not to express opinions on controversial issues, to avoid crowded places and to limit the time spent with family members.

The best of our sports journalism from the past seven days and a heads-up on the weekend’s action

Pinto was given 10 days’ warning, even though a decision had been taken in July, and the ruling’s implementation was suspended after it was established that he had not been given an opportunity to mount a challenge or appeal. He then appealed and is awaiting a final ruling.

In 2023 Pinto was given a suspended four-year prison sentence in Portugal for attempted extortion and cybercrime offences. He was acquitted in a second case involving similar charges two years later. The public prosecutor’s office and Benfica, one of the clubs hacked by Pinto, appealed against the ruling. A decision from the higher court is awaited.

Supporters regard Pinto as a whistleblower who cast light on corruption, whereas detractors argue that his tactics breached legal standards and moral principles. His disclosures reached far beyond football. Details involving magistrates, legal professionals and public officials were made public and he was the whistleblower behind Luanda Leaks, which exposed the inner workings of the business empire of Africa’s richest woman, Isabel dos Santos. She denied corruption allegations.

#913. McTominay reveals he had heart ‘shocked’ two days before World Cup opener

Midfielder was in hospital before Scotland v Haiti

‘I had to get the shock on my heart,’ says McTominay

Scott McTominay has revealed he was in hospital under sedation to have a “shock on my heart” just 48 hours before Scotland began their World Cup campaign against Haiti in June.

At the time McTominay’s absence from training was put down to a stomach complaint. It emerged in August that the Napoli midfielder needed surgery to remedy an irregular heartbeat. The operation took place in September, causing McTominay to miss Scotland’s first four Nations League matches. The player has now said the matter arose in the US as Scotland prepared for their World Cup opener at Boston Stadium.

McTominay is back in the international fold for Scotland’s fixtures against North Macedonia and Switzerland. Talking to media in Glasgow the 29-year-old said: “The World Cup was difficult for me to be honest. I had to go and get the shock on my heart. It was two days before the Haiti game and you have prepared so well. I was in such good condition and then something like that happens. And you think: ‘How is this happening to me?’ But then you have to get on with it.

“These are cards you are dealt in football. Sometimes things don’t go your way and you have to continue to do your best. It’s nowhere near an excuse but it’s something you have to look back on and say it’s part of the process.

“Whenever you are sitting in a hospital bed two days before the first game at the World Cup, about to get put to sleep it’s not ideal is it? When things like that happen it is what it is, there’s nothing you can do about it. After the World Cup I reflected on it and it’s probably the most disappointed I have been in my career.”

Scotland were knocked out in the group stage, with McTominay’s performances among those criticised. A poor campaign also led to the resignation of Steve Clarke as manager. Sébastien Pocognoli, Clarke’s successor, will call on McTominay for the first time when North Macedonia visit Hampden Park on Friday. McTom­inay returned to the Napoli team in early October. He has since scored five goals, including doubles against Bodø/Glimt and Roma. He sought to play down the significance of his heart problem.

“I’m feeling much, much better than what I was,” said McTominay. “It [the operation] was something that needed to be done. In your career you have moments like that, where things can take you by surprise. It looks a lot worse to people in the media and family or friends who reach out to you when they see news relating to a heart issue, but it was a relatively straightforward procedure which went really, really well in Manchester. I’m really happy to be back and playing football again.

“It was explained to me really well by the doctors at Napoli and my cardiologist in Manchester so the process was really straightforward. The doctor with Scotland when we were away at the World Cup explained, if that was going to be the case how it would look. All the staff members made me feel so relaxed about the situation.”

#911. Man Utd strike Poch agreement as Carrick takes training

Man Utd powerbrokers set to make a final decision on Michael Carrick's future at a Monaco summit on Wednesday having lined up Mauricio Pochettino, who has a £7m release clause in the contract he signed with the USA after the World Cup this past summer

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Manchester United have reached an agreement in principle with Mauricio Pochettino to take over as head coach if Michael Carrick is sacked.

Pochettino, currently in charge of the USA national team, is being lined up to potentially take over while Carrick is at Carrington taking training with the players that are not on international duty.

It is understood there are still details being finalised with Pochettino's camp while talks are set to accelerate with the US Soccer Federation (USSF) over when the Argentine can be released from his contract.

The £7m release clause in Pochettino's contract is not thought to be an issue for United. However, as things stand, Pochettino is due to take charge of the USA in games against Haiti on Saturday and Wednesday.

Once a solution can be found for those logistical hurdles, Pochettino is understood to be ready to take over if United ultimately decide to make a change at head coach, which remains likely.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

While Carrick is in Manchester at the training ground, United's powerbrokers are set to make a final decision on his future at a Monaco summit on Wednesday.

CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox had already been due to meet minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe for a summit to review the club's start to the season.

Scotland football news: Live updates, schedule and analysis of the national team

England: Jude and Jobe Bellingham train train together ahead of Croatia clash

Manchester United: Have club let Michael Carrick down?

Manchester United: Mauricio Pochettino's last game against the Red Devils when Chelsea boss

But with United in the relegation zone after their worst start to a league campaign for 40 years, Carrick's future is increasingly in doubt and expected to be decided at the meeting.

Berrada and Wilcox have to make their recommendation to Ratcliffe, who has control of football operations at Old Trafford, before a final decision is made over Carrick.

Carrick was handed a stay of execution after United's 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth in the Premier League last month, but momentum is now gathering behind a change in the dugout.

Pochettino has long been admired by United, who have held talks with the Argentine on at least two occasions about taking over.

Liverpool (A) - Premier League - Sunday November 22, live on Sky Sports

Sporting (A) - Champions League - Wednesday November 25

Brentford (H) - Premier League - Saturday November 28

Newcastle (A) - Premier League - Wednesday December 2, live on Sky Sports

Coventry (H) - Premier League - Saturday December 5

RB Leipzig (H) - Champions League - Tuesday December 8

Mauricio Pochettino and Manchester United have a well-established history. One where paths might have crossed long before now, numerous times, but somehow never managed to converge.

Could it be that we are finally to bear witness to the culmination of this elaborate 10-year dance of incompatible circumstances?

The Old Trafford hierarchy have always admired Pochettino from afar. He was on their radar while at Tottenham and again when it was clear his time at PSG was coming to an end. The Argentine was eventually lured back to the Premier League, but instead returned to London, signing with Chelsea.

All along this journey of complicated courtship, United were at play. There have been many sliding-door moments. At the time news broke of Chelsea's interest in Pochettino in 2023, United, coached by Erik ten Hag, had just been ripped to shreds by Sevilla.

The morning after that defeat all the back pages focussed on another humiliating capitulation in Europe. 'What the El was that?' one read. Another lay into the inadequacies of Harry Maguire's performance. No doubt both headlines have been recycled since. At United, the more things change, the more they stay the same.

Miraculously, it took another 18 months for the button to be pushed on Ten Hag. Four managers of varying permanency followed. Until another chance, a decade on from the first, has revealed itself to pursue the one that got away. Is this finally right place, right time for Pochettino?

Poch, nice guy by all accounts. But nice at United means nothing. He'll get eaten alive and spat out. United need a tough bloke to get under the skin of these over paid under performing players.

I don't think any manager in the world will get that team fighting for the title without serious change in recruitment and change at the top we'll be in exactly the same situation in 6-12 months time.

Another great manager who's going to end up being in the same scenario! Just another manager with the same results! It's the board! Not manager!

Why bring Poch when the issue are players with high salaries? Currently players have more say at a club then coaches. Players decide who they want to play for you can't make everyone happy.

Poch is the Argentine Carrick. What's he going to do any different to Carrick? And Wilcox will be loving it knowing he wont have to buy any players and Poch will just use the youth players. Another circus show about to begin.

Poch is a very good manager, would be very happy with him at United. The fans saying he's not good enough need to stop living in the past. We no longer attract world class managers and let's be honest there's only about 5 left in football.

Right choice about 10 managers ago… which elite club would appoint him now?

#908. 'A beautiful story' as Bellingham brothers called up

Jude and Jobe Bellingham could be the first brothers to play together for England since Gary and Phil Neville 19 years ago

It may be a surprise to some but Jobe Bellingham's call-up to the England senior side has been a long time coming.

The 21-year-old's career path has been very similar to that of his 23-year-old brother Jude - England's star player at the World Cup and one of Real Madrid's best players. Both were stars of the Birmingham City academy before big-money moves to the German Bundesliga and England call-ups.

Jobe's debut for Birmingham came at the age of 16 years and 107 days - 69 days older than Jude when he made his first appearance for the Blues' senior side.

The central midfielder then moved to Sunderland and helped them win promotion to the Premier League before joining German side Borussia Dortmund at the age of 19 in a deal worth up to Â£31m.

Jude also moved to Dortmund when he was 17, before developing into one of the world's best players and joining Real Madrid.

Having one of the best midfielders in the world as your older brother comes with challenges and Jobe has consistently been compared to his sibling.

But the former Sunderland midfielder is his own player, wearing 'Jobe' on the back of his shirt instead of his family name. He said it was suggested to him by a former coach because "it shows that I'm going my own way".

England manager Thomas Tuchel told BBC Radio 5 Live it is "a beautiful story".

"They are both good for each other," he added. "My understanding is they are very close.

"It makes life easier for Jobe to come into camp and know his brother is one of the key players in our team. So, that will hopefully help him, but don't forget he is here on his own merits, and he is not here because of his brother."

Jobe is a different type of player to Jude, sitting deeper in the midfield, but is as physically imposing while still being good on the ball.

He is the current captain of the England Under-21 side, and Tuchel said Young Lions head coach Lee Carsley had been pushing for some time for the younger Bellingham to get senior recognition.

"He's the standout player," said Tuchel. "He's the captain, so the door should always be open for the pathway, always be open for special performances over a long period of time.

"That's what Jobe has done on top of it. He found his way, he found his rhythm with Dortmund. He's had an excellent start to his season, is a regular starter and influential."

Thomas Tuchel on Jobe Bellingham's England call-up

England host Croatia at Wembley on Thursday, 12 November before travelling to Madrid to take on Spain on 15 November in this next international break.

With Arsenal's Myles Lewis-Skelly suspended for the first game, and Bournemouth's Alex Scott out injured after shining on his debut in last month's 7-0 win over Croatia, Tuchel said a natural "opportunity" for Jobe had opened up.

"He deserves to make an impression for us," said the German in his news conference after naming the squad.

"It's an incredible achievement for the family and for the brothers. I saw his excitement straight away and his smile.

"He has an open and calm personality. He's one of five players for the central midfield.

"He's a more defensive player than Jude. So strong on the ball, good physique, a big body, a very physical player and can keep possession.

"It's now up to him, but he's excited and happy and eager to impress, and that's the best foundation to have a good camp for him."

Jude shared a throwback photo of him and Jobe after Friday's squad announcement

If they get on the pitch together, Jude and Jobe won't be the first brothers to represent the Three Lions.

It has been 19 years since Gary and Phil Neville, who both played for Manchester United, last played together for England, and 30 years since they started.

They first played together for England in 1996 against China, becoming the first siblings to do so since Bobby and Jack Charlton 26 years earlier.

Jack and Bobby were both part of England's 1966 World Cup-winning squad.

Bobby was the younger of the two, but made his Three Lions debut first. He went on to win 106 international caps.

Jack, who was not called into the England team until days before his 30th birthday, won 35 caps.

More recently, brothers Nathaniel and Trevoh Chalobah have both played for England, but never alongside each other.

Nathaniel made his solitary appearance as an injury-time substitute in a 3-2 away win against Spain in a 2018 Nations League game.

His younger brother Trevoh, currently a Como defender, made the first of his three international appearances against Senegal in June 2025 and was in England's 2026 World Cup squad.

Bobby and Jack Charlton were both in the England squad that lifted the Jules Rimet Trophy at Wembley.

The Chalobah brothers never played together for England, but both featured for the senior side.

Jobe Bellingham has made 14 appearances for Dortmund this season

Jobe has shown remarkable progress since last winter. In the first couple of months, following his move from Sunderland to Borussia Dortmund, he seemed timid, as if he was just trying to avoid making any mistakes. His passes rarely, if ever, caused trouble for opposing defences.

Even Dortmund manager Niko Kovac said at one point that he was surprised how long it might take him to get comfortable in the Bundesliga. But hard work in the gym to build up muscle mass in order to become more explosive and the fact that he received plenty of chances in Dortmund's line-up has helped his development.

In the latter stages of last season, his decision-making was much faster and his intensity seemed higher. Still, Dortmund decided to sign Dutch midfielder Joey Veerman, a specialist at making line-breaking passes, in August.

It meant Jobe's place in the starting XI was far from secure at the beginning of this season.

In recent games, Kovac has employed Bellingham in a more advanced role, as one of the two number 10s behind the striker. In this role, Bellingham drove into the final third with pace and showed intensity during pressing sequences.

His performance in the 2-2 draw against Bayern Munich in the Bundesliga last Saturday was arguably his best since his arrival in Germany.

#907. Love Island’s Trinity Reveals Living Situation With Bryce in L.A.

Trinity Tatum exclusively told E! News at the 2026 EBONY Power 100 what her and Bryce Alakai’s life together in L.A. looks like after their Love Island USA win: “I make him come over all the time.”

Trinity Tatum and Bryce Alakai’s romance was never meant to stay in Fiji.

In fact, Tatum recently moved from her native Virginia to Los Angeles, where Alakai is based, following their win on Love Island USA season eight—and their new chapter is going swimmingly.

“I just got my apartment,” she exclusively told E! News in a joint interview with fellow islander Aniya Harvey at the 2026 EBONY Power 100 event on Nov. 9. “But it’s so funny because I literally just spent the night over Bryce’s house last night, so it’s like do a combination of I go over his house, he comes over mine.”

For them, having that balance in their relationship is crucial.

“He’s like, ‘I’m paying rent. I still have to go home,’” the 23-year-old quipped. “I make him come over all the time and he’s like, ‘Girl, I’m still paying rent to be here. L.A. rent is not cheap, honey.’”

That’s why Tatum and Alakai, 30, have “been mixing and dabbling” to get a "mix of both.” And the life they’ve built is exactly her type on paper.

“I’ve been in L.A. a lot,” she continued. “I’ve been around my man. I’ve been around all his friends and all of my girls.”

As for their holiday plans, the two will be making a splash with their loved ones.

“I am spending the holidays in Boston,” Tatum shared. “I want to spend a lot of it with my mom. We’re both spending it with both of our families.”

And Harvey is keen to do the same. After all, she revealed her plans to throw a huge holiday party in her native Atlanta, sharing she’ll be inviting “every single person.”

And that of course includes the rest of the core four ladies, including Kayda Bosse and Melanie Moreno, who Tatum shared she still talks to daily.

And Harvey, 24, makes it a point to stay connected as well. As she put it, “I feel like we do a good job of being in tune with one another.”

But in addition to finding both love and friendship in the Villa, the core four have also found success, a fact that Tatum shared they still “process” every day.

“I feel like every time we go to an event like this or anything we’ve been invited to, we are processing it,” she said. “Like, wow we’re really here.”

And Harvey echoed that sentiment, adding, “We take it in every single day. It’s such a blessing.”

Keep reading for a closer look at where more Love Island couples stand today…

Nathan Massey & Cara De La Hoyde: Married

The ultimate Love Island success story, Nathan and Cara were declared season two's winning pair after meeting in the villa in 2016.

Once Cara learned she was pregnant with their first child in May 2017, the couple briefly split before reconciling and welcoming their son, Freddie, in December 2017. Nathan proposed to Cara in July 2018, bringing her back to the place where it all began—the villa, of course—to pop the question.

The duo exchanged vows in June 2019 and welcomed their second child, daughter Delilah, in July 2020.

After coming in second place on UK's second season in 2016, Alex and Olivia got engaged the following year, with Olivia even appearing on an episode of Say Yes to the Dress to find her dream wedding gown.

The season two pair exchanged vows in a September 2018 ceremony, with their wedding process and life as newlyweds being documented for TLC's Olivia and Alex Said Yes and then Olivia and Alex: Happily Ever After.

Alex and Olivia welcomed their son Abel in June 2022 and announced in February 2025 they're expecting Baby No. 2. Daughter Sienna arrived that August.

Dom and Jess proved to be one of the series' strongest love stories, continuing their relationship after he was voted off the show.

UK's season three couple wed in October 2018 and share two children.

Just when viewers were worried all hope was lost for season three fan-favorite Camilla, Jamie entered late in the game and it was clear who he had shown up for. Swoon.

While they ultimately finished in second, Camilla and Jamie have been going strong ever since their first meeting in 2017. The couple married in September 2021 and share three kids: Nell (born in October 2020), Nora (May 2022) and Brodie (May 2024).

The Love Island UK season four contestants may have left the villa together in 2018, but their romance fizzled out not long after returning from Mallorca. They have since gone their separate ways.

Ellie announced in July 2025 that she had gotten engaged to her boyfriend, whose name she has not publicly announced, one year after debuting their relationship.

Months after Dani and Jack were crowned the champions of Love Island season four, they announced their breakup.

"Jack and I have sadly decided to part ways," Dani wrote on Instagram in December 2018. "It's been an incredible six months, and we will always have a place in our hearts for each other, but we've sadly come to the realisation that it's not meant to be long term. We both plan to stay friends.”

They ended up being more than friends and soon rekindled their romance. But by early 2019, they’d split again—with Jack noting on Instagram "sometimes things aren’t meant to be."

"We will always care a lot for each other and have love for each other," he added in an April 2019 post, "and I mean that from the bottom of my heart and I wish her nothing but happiness."

Jack noted he and Dani “really did try to make it work but it unfortunately didn’t and that is life.” Years later, he shared his battle with addiction contributed to their split.

"I have blown more than a million pounds thanks to drugs, booze and gambling," Jack told The Sun in February 2025. "Drugs helped my relationship with Dani fail. I was absent, my priorities were wrong, I wasn’t a great boyfriend. I am determined to change my future."

Meanwhile, Dani has found love with soccer player Jarrod Bowen, whom she wed in May 2025. Together, they share twin girls Summer and Star, who were born in May 2023. Dani is also mom to Santi, the son she welcomed with ex Sammy Kimmence in January 2021.

Lucie and Joe first paired up on day one of season five. But when he was voted out of the villa, she quickly moved on by dating multiple other men (and admitting to having serious feelings for a taken Tommy). So it was quite the surprise for fans when they revealed they were dating after their season ended.

But just like their initial romance, the surfer and the sandwich maker's second attempt fizzled out, with the couple splitting in early December 2019.

And while Lucie is now engaged to season six's Luke, Joe (despite shooting his shot on All Stars in 2024) seems to be enjoying the single life.

Sigh, this one stung. Don't you just hate it when the winning couple is one of the first ones to split? After getting together just weeks before the finale, with Greg being one of the last Islanders to join the villa, the fan-favorite pair managed to win season five. But they broke up just weeks later.

After some mild controversy and back and forth between the couple over how exactly the split went down (apparently Greg, a rugby player based in Ireland, ended it via text), Amber said on Loose Women, "I think the careers and the distance was always a factor. It was always something that we knew about, so I don't know what changed. I kind of wanted to make it work, but it is what it is, really."

As for Greg, he defended himself, saying on RTE's The Late Late Show, "She lives in the UK, every brand wants to work with her, every event wants her there, of course, she deserves all of it and I decided to come back to Ireland and do my thing here."

However, he found a new connection and kicked off 2025 by proposing to his love Jeanni Mulder.

While they were the second season five couple to call it quits soon after their time in the villa came to an end, Anton and Belle remained friends, though he ruled out any chance of a romantic rekindling.

"No, definitely not, it's just not that type of relationship," the fitness app creator told Mail Online. "We're so friendly now, it would be like dating your sister, effectively. It's not that kind of relationship anymore."

In 2024, Anton appeared on Love Island: All Stars, where he came in fifth with Georgia Harrison. However, they soon split.

Molly-Mae Hague & Tommy Fury: Back Together

After a dramatic start to their romance, the Instagram influencer and the boxer quickly became season five's most solid couple...which was why it was so surprising when they came in second.

They got engaged in July 2024—exactly six months after the birth of their daughterBambi—but Molly-Mae dropped a breakup bombshell in August 2024.

"I’m extremely upset to announce that mine and Tommy’s relationship has come to an end," she shared on Instagram Stories. "I will forever be grateful for the most important thing to me, now and always, my beautiful daughter. Without us, there would be no her. She will always be my priority."

But on a May 2025 episode of her Amazon Prime seriesMolly-Mae: Behind It All, she revealed that she and Tommy weregiving their relationship another chance.After announcingshe was expecting their second babyin February 2026, Molly-Mae and Tommy became parents of two in June 2026.

Arguably one of season five's most polarizing pairs after enduring their fair share of drama, the fourth-place finishers proved their doubters wrong by taking their relationship beyond the villas in 2019.

"I think trust one another, don't believe everything you read in the press and one main thing: Don't let fame get to your head," Maura said on UK's This Morning of how they've made their relationship work. "You just need to stay grounded."

However, the pair broke up in March 2020.

"Curtis and I have made the decision to separate," Maura wrote in a note posted to her Instagram Stories. "We enjoyed a great experience from our time in the villa and want to thank everyone for supporting our relationship."But that wasn't the end of Curtis' Love Island journey. After a short run on Love Island: Games in 2023, he appeared on Love Island: All Stars two years later, where he and Ekin-Su came in third place. However, the two called it quits a few months later.

"I wanted to share that Curtis and I have decided to go our separate ways," Ekin-Su announced in a May 2025 Instagram post, per People. "It's been a really tough decision, but one made with a lot of love and respect for one another," she wrote in a post on her Instagram Stories. "He's an incredible person and I'll always cherish the memories we made both in and out of the villa."

While they got together later than a majority of the couples in the villa (with the fan-favorite Ovie making his debut during the infamous Casa Amor episodes and India joining even later), the pair made it to the finals, coming in third place for season five in 2019.

However, the professional basketball player and the model quietly parted ways later that year.

"Obviously it's difficult, but any break up is difficult," she told the MailOnline. "It's even more difficult when it's in front of the rest of the world, but I'll be fine. I'm lucky I've got a really close group of girlfriends, they've been really looking after me."

In early 2025, India appeared on Love Island: All Stars but left the show single.

The winners of the first-ever winter season of Love Island coupled up almost immediately, staying together despite all of the obstacles the villa presented.

They moved in together after the season ended in February 2020, but called it quits three years later.

'We're still really good friends," Paige shared during a June 2023 appearance on Love Island: After Sun. "I think we drifted apart."But in August 2024, Finley debuted a new romance on Instagram. And while the couple initially kept her identity private, The Sun confirmed in June 2025 he's dating Jess Hale. They welcomed their son Austin in January 2026.

One season six's most unexpected couples came in third place during the winter-set run, though they split a couple of months after leaving the villa.

"We've completely called it off now. I think it was brought about more from his behalf than mine, but we're mutual and friendly," Demi told MailOnline in June 2020. "With lockdown, it drove us apart and we live so far away from each other. I feel like there wasn't a lot of effort made with communication, so we drifted as a result."

Luke has since coupled up with season five's blonde bombshell Lucie Donlan, with the pair confirming their romance in July 2020. They got engaged the following year.

As for Demi, she appeared on Love Island: All Stars in 2024, where she met Luis Morrison. However, they broke up later that year.

Season six's low-key pair came in fourth place, going on to date for several months before breaking up in June 2020.

"To confirm, myself and Ched have split, we are still good friends and I wish him all the best x," Jess informed her Instagram followers. "Thanks for all the support you have given us since the villa."

While he started off season six as a fan-favorite, Nas ended up losing support after breaking things off with Demi Jones to be with Eva post-Casa Amor.

Nas and Eva, however, remained together despite being voted off the show, and they made their relationship official in July 2020.

Though they sparked engagement rumors in August 2023, when Eva was spotted with a ring on that finger, Nas confirmed in March 2024 that the pair had parted ways.

"Unfortunately, Eva and I have decided to end our relationship," Nas wrote on Instagram Story. "There is no bad blood or wrong doing—it was a mutual and completely amicable decision."

He added, "We tried to work things out over the past couple of months but decided this was for the best, and are both at peace with the situation."

Nas went on to appear on Love Island: All Stars in early 2025, but ultimately left the villas solo.

The scaffolder became one of the most hated men in the U.K. when he dumped fan-favorite Shaughna Phillips for Molly during his stay at Casa Amor, with the public eventually voting the pair out of the villa.

And while the two stayed together for three years off the island, they went their separate ways in 2023.

The following year, they both went on Love Island: All Stars. Molly coupled up with Tom Clare, and they were declared the winners of the season. Meanwhile, Callum formed a romance with Jess Gale and they were the runners-up. And while Callum and Jess split later in 2024 (with him now dating Yasmin Deplidge), Molly and Tom are still going strong.

Winter Love Island's 2020 runner-ups Siânnise and Luke found love in the villa and went on to date for about a year before breaking up in November 2021.

However, he's since found love again and got engaged to Chelsea Menna less than a year later in 2022.

Millie Court & Liam Reardon: Split (Again)

The season seven Love Island UK champs brought their love story out of the villa and into the real world in August 2021, after their loyalty was put to the test in Casa Amor.

They announced their breakup on social media in July 2022, but reconciled almost a year later. For a stretch, Millie and Liam continue to provide glimpses into their life together on social media—posting about their travels, workouts and dates—and on their eponymous podcast. But the pair split for a second time in the fall of 2025.

Ekin-Su Cülcüloglu & Davide Sanclimenti: Split

Nearly a year after Ekin-Su and Davide were declared the winners of Love Island season eight in 2022, he announced they'd parted ways.

"@ekinsuofficial & I are no longer together," he wrote on Instagram in June 2023 "I am grateful for the memories and opportunities we shared together and I wish her nothing but the best. I would like for everybody to respect this decision during this difficult time. I will continue to support Ekin in anyway possible."

Not long after, the pair rekindled their romance. However, they ended up calling it quits again.

Both opened their hearts up to love again. In the summer of 2024, Davide began dating Iris Au. Meanwhile, Ekin-Su briefly dated Curtis outside the villas after they placed third on Love Island: All Stars in early 2025. However, they split months later.

The Love Island UK couple walked away from the villa as winners on season 10, but called it quits just two months later in October 2023.

According to Sammy, the breakup came as a "total shock."

"We had a private conversation but this was left up in the air as Jess is still away and we haven't had a chance to speak in person," he wrote in an Instagram Story at the time. "To be totally clear—I at least wanted to see if our relationship could be saved and felt this would be the respectful way forward."

Sammy added, "Despite how all this has played out today, I think Jess is an amazing woman and genuinely wish her the best."

In early 2025, Sammy appeared on Love Island: All Stars, where he formed a relationship with Elma Pazar. But in June 2025, the two sparked split rumors.

The couple first met on Love Island UK's season 11, with Uma leaving on day 37 with Wil when he was dumped from the island after she was chosen by Reuben Collins.

In July 2025, one year after leaving together, Uma announced that she and Wil were engaged. She wrote on Instagram with her ring on display, "We've been sitting on a bad boy piece of information."

For the reality star, staying on Love Island after Wil's exit didn't seem like an option.

"There was no question. I didn't have to think about it at all," she said of her decision on the Not My Bagg podcast. "I want to be with Wil."

"I've met someone," she explained to hosts Lisa Baggs and Joe Baggs. "It takes me so long to get to the position I was with Wil, to be so comfortable with someone. There were two weeks left. What was I gonna do? Just sit there and fake a new connection? I'd rather just be honest."

Josh Ritchie & Sophie Piper: Still Together

Both Josh and Sophie had tried to find their matches on Love Island before (he came in third place with Lauren Richardson in 2015; she checked into the villas five years later). But the stars seemed to align when they appeared on Love Island: All Stars in 2024, finishing third.

"Just the beginning," she wrote on Instagram that February. "Thank you so much to everyone that has supported us throughout our journey honestly means the world."

And she was correct that it was only the start of their forever journey.

"Our first year anniversary," Josh wrote on Instagram in March 2025. "I don’t know how you have put up with me for this long. You have a life time of this so I hope you no what you have a signed up for. Love you always."

The winners of the inaugural season of Love Island USA (who paired up on day one and never parted) dated for several months before calling it quits at the end of 2019. "The breakup was mutual and we have left on amicable terms," Zac wrote on his Instagram Stories. "We simply wanted different things."

In her own statement, Elizabeth added, "Although I had wished things could've turned out differently life doesn't always work out the way we could've hoped sometimes."

However, she found love again—getting engaged to Gianni Settino in December 2024.

"For everyone watching Love Island USA right now," she captioned a July 2024 Instagram post, "yes I have recoupled 5 years later."

The season one Love Island USA runners-up dated for several months before calling it quits in late November 2019, posting statements on their respective Instagram Stories. "Alex and I are no longer together," the lacrosse coach shared. "Sometimes it just doesn't work out."

Alex explained that "heartbreak is hard," adding, "Our story was a Fairytale romance for me, but sometimes things just don't work out."

While they didn't win Love Island USA's first season, the fan-favorite couple tried making long-distance work, traveling to spend the holidays together. However, Caro publicly announced that she ended the relationship in a July 2020 YouTube video. "I just don't feel like he was committed to the relationship like I was," she said. "So that's why I decided to break up with him."

But in October 2023, Caro dropped an exciting new bombshell: She wed Rene Lacad the month before. And that December, she revealed that she and her new husband were expecting a baby girl. Their daughter Amina arrived in April 2024.

"Note to Amina: Thank you for making me your mama," she wrote on Instagram in a Mother's Day 2025 post. "Nothing in this life tops that."

Despite the other couples in the villa and most of America not fully believing in their future, season one USA pair Weston and Emily managed to date IRL for a bit before going their separate ways.

"Weston and I are no longer together," she confirmed in a May 2020 YouTube video. "I am single. Basically we kind of went through a roller coaster of a journey together…. It was really hard with distance especially because I was in college."

The delivered one of the U.S. version's most unexpected couplings, with Kyra choosing to leave the show during the inaugural season to see if she still had a shot with Cashel after sending him home…only to find out he'd already returned. But, unfortunately, the musically inclined couple split in October 2019.

By the end of November, they had reconciled. However, Kyra and Cashel ended their relationship for good in February 2020.

"We had a good go," he said on the #NoFilter podcast. "I think we're just in different places in our lives...I think she blocked my number, to be honest."

Kyra went on to appear on other shows including Match Me If You Can in 2021, The Challenge: USA in 2022 (which Cashel also competed on) and Love Island Games in 2023. But she ended up finding her match off-camera with dental student and former basektball player Tal Sahar in 2024.

In May 2025, Cashel was jailed in Utah on charges of domestic violence and assault, according to online records. The following month, new charges of assault and domestic violence were filed against him.

Cely Vazquez & Johnny Middlebrooks: Split

While the pair found love on season two of Love Island USA, which aired in the summer of 2020, they announced their breakup the following January.

Kordell Beckham & Serena Page: Still Together

Among Kordell and Serena's many long-term goals? Sticking together.

And the Love Island USA season six winners are still very much in love.

"Happiest of birthdays to the literal man of my dreams," Serena wrote on Instagram for Kordell’s birthday in May 2025, "almost 1 year later and I cannot believe how obsessed I still am with you. Its so amazing to watch you grow and your dreams come true in real time, I am so so proud of the man you are growing into more and more everyday and cannot wait to spend more birthdays with you!! Thank you for being the best boyfriend, partner, friend, and making me the happiest girl ever."
