#905. 'The worst conditions in my 35-year career' - commentating in the FA Cup fog

Notts County beat Altrincham in incredible fog-filled spectacle

One of the most important attributes for a commentator is to be able to see the action you are trying to describe but that became a luxury for BBC Sport's Steve Bower when Altrincham hosted Notts County in an FA Cup tie on Saturday.

As thick fog enveloped the Moss Lane ground, he could barely see what was going on in a first-round game being televised live on BBC Two.

"One of the more challenging of my long career, that's about 35 years now," said Bower about the experience.

"I was reminded by a colleague - maybe I'm a jinx - that we had a similar thing on the BBC about three years ago when we did York against Wigan in the second round and the fog came in.

"Tonight was worse. From where we were, opposite the dugouts, once the play went to the centre circle and beyond, we couldn't see a thing.

"We couldn't see which team had the ball, let alone which player had the ball after about the 60th minute. Bearing in mind it went to extra-time, it was challenging.

"I just kept looking down at my phone and it was text message after text message from people saying, 'You're sounding great, but I can't see a thing'. In the end, you have to roll with it and do the best you can."

Notts County progress in FA Cup tie no-one could see

'It's like a fever dream' - commentators struggle through fog

National League Altrincham were on for an upset when they took a 2-1 lead against the League One side but a late Callum Roberts equaliser for County took the game to extra-time before the visiting side won on penalties.

"The frustrating thing is that for an hour it was a really good FA Cup tie, it had everything," said Bower.

"It was on for another giant-killing script but then the frustrating thing is that it becomes a non-event because, without stating the obvious, people can't see half of it.

"Also, it's not then about the tactics, or the shape of it, or the aggression, or the effort because you just can't see it. As a spectacle in trying to describe a game like you normally would, it's impossible."

Bower's radio colleagues were not faring much better as they tried to work out what was going on.

"I can just about see the bright white numbers on their shirts, but I am struggling to see what is happening on the far side of the pitch," said BBC Radio Nottingham commentator Adam Hassell.

Former Notts County striker Mark Stallard, who was also speaking on BBC Radio Nottingham, said: "We're looking around, and here in the press box no-one knows where the ball is! It's like a spot-the-ball competition.

"I played in the Notts County cup side against Wimbledon when it was abandoned - they equalised in the second half and I didn't see any of it!"

Stallard later said: "We genuinely cannot see the linesman or the players on the far side. It's slightly farcical having to commentate for radio listeners."

Altrincham have a rich history of causing FA Cup upsets but could not add to that in the fog against Notts County

The managers of both teams were on the touchline but even they were struggling as tactics went out of the window.

"[Notts County boss] Martin Paterson said credit to Altrincham, they were the better team in the first half and, as for the second, I couldn't see it. He was laughing," said Bower.

"Neil Gibson, the Altrincham manager, was saying, 'We were trying to get down to pitchside to look tactically at what they had done after those four substitutions. Have they changed shape? Is it a back four? Have they gone to a box midfield? But we just couldn't see'.

"So even from a tactical point of view, the players had to stop playing long diagonal passes and things like that because they couldn't see, they were just having to play short five, 10 yard passes so the game changed in that sense as well.

"It was very, very close to getting called off."

Bower said some of the players told him they couldn't see both goals or the corner flags from the centre circle.

"It will live long in the memory, that's for sure," said Bower. "Even on the penalties, you were having to rely on the crowd's reaction before committing to the tale.

"You couldn't see the goalkeeper's save, for instance, until the first replay came in."

The penalties took place in front of Altrincham fans and, while Bower had replays to call on, the Notts County fans "couldn't have seen anything" from the other end as they had to go on "crowd reaction".

"Obviously, the Altrincham fans all had their phones on with the lights trying to put the Notts County players off as well in the fog. A unique evening all around."

#903. Mormon Wives' Jen Affleck Says She's "Not Doing the Best" Amid Divorce

Jen Affleck, who stars on Hulu’s upcoming Nov. 12 series Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County, shared insight into her priorities amid her and Zac Affleck’s divorce.

Jen Affleck is swinging into a new chapter.

After filing for divorce from husband Zac Affleck, the Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County star shared insight into how she’s navigating her new normal.

“I'm not doing the best right now,” Jen—who is currently pregnant with her and Zac’s fourth baby—admitted to E! News in an exclusive interview. “I'm just taking one day at a time, and really just focusing on my kids. And obviously, the timing sucks, especially with me being pregnant.”

Nevertheless, she affirmed, “Ultimately, it was the best decision for us.”

And with that right decision bolstering her sails, Jen enjoyed sailing into the new horizon alongside her Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County costars Bobbi Althoff, Aspyn Ovard, Avery Woods, Madison Bontempo, McCall DaPron, Salomé Andrea, Ashleigh Pease and Jordan McClanahan.

For the Dancing With the Stars alum, the timing of filming Orange County made to an experience that was more freeing than her seasons on Secret Lives of Mormon Wives.

“What's funny is there was no reinventing this time,” the 27-year-old admitted. “I just showed up as me. I feel like for the past seven, eight years of my life, I've tried to mold myself into who I think people want to see, whether it be for my marriage or for TV or for the world. And this year was the first time that I really felt like I was reclaiming my identity and who I actually am.”

So, “going into the season, I just poured my heart into it,” she added. “Nothing was storyline; everything was real.”

That meant allowing the cameras to track her difficult chapter as it played out.

“I'm obviously not excited for people to see all the painful parts of the show,” she continued, “but I'm looking forward to people seeing the real, real me—and I guess I'm still trying to figure out who the real me is as well. So, we'll see that unfold in the future.”

As for how Jen showed up to The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County, fans can tune in for the premiere on Thursday, November 12 on Hulu and Hulu on Disney+.

While Jen has in large part remained publicly silent on her divorce—though she did share two videos from her and Zac’s relationship, highlighting his less-than-ideal behavior—Zac shared a five-minute video sharing insight into their split.

“This is something we've been talking about for a long time,” he said of their breakup in the Nov. 5 TikTok. “Jen came to me about a year ago, after Dancing With the Stars, and told me she was unhappy and wanted a divorce. And I basically begged her to stay, told her I’d work on things, fix things, become whoever she needed me to be."

It was during this time that Jen became pregnant with their fourth baby, who will join siblings Nora, 5, Luca, 3, and Penelope, 16 months.

And, much like Jen, Zac wants to make sure their children remain his and her priority.

"That's really my priorities," he shared. "I feel like probably the thing that's eating me alive the most is I feel like I failed my kids, and I'm worried that I'm going to cause them damage. And I just hope that we can still give them a normal childhood, but as far as that goes, Jen and I are definitely on the same page of wanting to give them the best the best life we can."

As for why their marriage came to an end, he reflected, “Marriage is hard. Having your marriage in the public is hard. Raising kids is hard. And I think slowly over time we lost that spark."

Meanwhile, for a closer look at where Jen and Zac’s SLOMW: OC costars stand in their love lives, read on. And don’t miss the premiere of The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County on Nov. 12.

Following her divorce from Cory Althoff, podcaster Bobbi Althoff is dating Tyler Hawkins, who plays a special role in Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County.

"He styles me, that’s how he supports me,” she told E! News in May, adding that the basketball player, "picks out my outfits every day. He styles me every day for the show. It’s great."

Aspyn Ovard, who filed for divorce from Parker Ferris in 2024 after eight years of marriage, is currently in a throuple relationship with married couple Billy Davis and Bri Davis.

After many ups and downs, Jen Affleck—who is pregnant with her and Zac Affleck's fourth baby—officially filed for divorce from her husband of seven years, E! News confirmed Nov. 4.

Despite ongoing relationship speculation, Salomé Andrea and Aaron Brimhall are still going strong as they prepare to welcome their third baby together. The duo, who married in 2012, also share 8-year-old twins Luca and Rue.

McCall DaPron—the sister of Mormon Wives' Mayci Neeley—shares four kids with husband Kirk DaPron, who she wed in 2011.

Ashleigh Pease and Nate Pease are rock solid after over a decade of marriage. "This 13th year together is one that has felt full circle!" she wrote on Instagram in September. "A season of fruits. Comfort. The happiest milestones."

Madison Bontempo and Kyler Steven Fisher, who wed in 2013, have been open about the highs and lows of their relationship. "Kyler and I aren’t perfect," she wrote on Instagram in October. "We’ve had arguments. We’ve had hard seasons. We’ve had moments we wish we could take back. And we’re not afraid to admit that."

But, she added, "Those moments aren’t our whole story. There’s also laughter, friendship, forgiveness, growth, five beautiful children, a million memories, and a love that has continued to evolve through every season of our lives."

Avery Woods and David Woods, parents to Ziggy and Stevie, are still feeling the love after a decade of marriage. As she simply put it, "my forever + always."

#902. Alcaraz and Zverev headline the ATP Finals in Turin - live on Sky Sports

Alexander Zverev chases a third crown at the season-ending tournament, while Carlos Alcaraz targets his first with Ben Shelton, Daniil Medvedev and Frances Tiafoe also involved; The ATP Finals from Turin is live on Sky Sports Tennis from 15-22 November

The climax to the 2025 ATP Tour season is upon us again with the season-ending ATP Finals set for Turin, live on Sky Sports Tennis.

World No 1 Alexander Zverev is chasing his third crown at the event, while Carlos Alcaraz will try to lift the trophy in Turin for the first time.

Ben Shelton, Daniil Medvedev, Flavio Cobolli, Arthur Fils, Frances Tiafoe and Rafael Jodar make up the field.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

The tournament has been contested in major cities around the world, with a rich history dating back to the birth of The Masters in Tokyo (1970), and continues this year at Turin's Inalpi Arena.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

The Nitto ATP Finals is structured as a round-robin format, with eight singles players/doubles teams divided into two groups of four.

All singles matches are the best of three tie-break sets. All doubles matches are best of three sets, with the first two sets played as tie-break sets with no ads and the final set played as a match tie-break.

The top seeded player/team is placed in Group A and the second seeded player/team is placed in Group B. The remaining players/teams are then drawn in pairs with the first drawn placed in Group A and the second drawn placed in Group B.

Each player/team plays the three other players/teams in his group.

The winner of each group is placed in separate semi-final brackets, with the top player/team in Group A playing the runner-up in Group B, and vice versa.

#901. 'I can't believe he is one of us' - inside Salah's life in Trabzon

Mohamed Salah has scored 10 goals in 15 games for Turkish club Trabzonspor

Back in August, when Mohamed Salah landed in Istanbul after flying in from his holiday in Mykonos, he wore Trabzonspor's burgundy and blue home strip as he stepped out of the plane to be greeted by thousands of fans.

That kit sold out almost instantly. Later that day, as Salah headed to Trabzon in north-east Turkey to complete the formalities of one of the most unexpected transfers after the expiry of his Liverpool contract, he asked one of his entourage what he should wear.

"The same kit," came the response, but Trabzonspor president Ertugrul Dogan advised Salah to wear the black away kit instead. Of course, that sold out too.

From the outset of the 34-year-old's arrival to this historic port city on the Black Sea, that sense of adulation has only grown.

"I went to the airport to see him in Istanbul and it was surreal," says Nisa Dumangoz. "I still can't believe that he is one of us."

Go for a stroll through Trabzon on matchday and it is Salah's face which adorns everything. Even the walls inside the fishmongers have pictures of him.

At the club shop in town, one of the staff jokes that the ground floor is for the Egyptian and the upper floor is for everything else.

Outside the stadium, there are scarves, magnets, keyrings, lighters with his face on and Egyptian Nemes headdresses in Trabzonspor colours. Season ticket sales rocketed after his arrival.

"Walking around Trabzon, it feels as though nine out of every 10 fans wearing a shirt have Salah's name on the back. The 10th has their own," says Turkish football journalist Hasan Tuncel.

The club have surpassed their merchandise revenue from last year in three months since Salah's arrival, while the local airport is only getting busier.

Liverpool was difficult to reach for many supporters across the Arab world and tickets were often hard to source. Trabzon is far more accessible, with new flights introduced from Cairo, Dubai and Riyadh since Salah's arrival.

On our flight from Istanbul, we meet an Egyptian family of 10 coming from Cairo for Trabzonspor's Uefa Conference League game against Freiburg.

"He is our ambassador and our Egyptian King, and with how many people want to come to Turkey now, he is their ambassador too," says Mahmoud.

At the game, there is a group of Egyptian celebrities and influencers. A quick check of their social media shows their combined Instagram following of about five million. Trabzonspor have three million. Salah has 68 million.

Salah recently went for a hike and posed for a picture on a rock in the Trabzon highlands. That rock has been renamed Salahtasi (Salah's Rock) and is now a tourist destination.

The commercial element of his signing has more than been justified but crucially, on the pitch, Salah is driving Trabzonspor's push for the Turkish Super Lig title and he has hit the ground running with 10 goals and five assists in all competitions.

Trabzonspor trail leaders Galatasaray by three points, having won seven of their first 10 games, including victories against the table-toppers and Besiktas.

For context, the Istanbul 'big three' of Galatasaray (26), Fenerbahce (19) and Besiktas (16) have won the league on 61 occasions combined, compared with Trabzonspor's seven titles.

"In Turkey, he is the biggest football star after Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo," says Kerim Tonyali, who is part of Gurbetci Gencler, a Trabzonspor supporters' group.

And given Salah's status as an icon, Trabzonspor are quickly becoming the second club for many in Turkey and the wider Muslim world.

Salah's face is a common sight wherever you go in Trabzon

Trabzon may be more than 2,000 miles from Liverpool but there are similarities, particularly when it comes to the sense of identity and pride associated with originating from here.

"Everywhere is Trabzon for us," is the local mantra and aligns with the sense of unity within this city that has a population of about 800,000 and is only the 30th-biggest in Turkey.

For Salah, the financials were important and he is earning about Â£14.6m per year as well as 20% of official merchandise sold with his name on, but one of the key aspects of coming here was the ability to focus entirely on his football.

Besiktas was considered as an option after the 2026 World Cup but, after multiple calls with Trabzonspor, Salah felt they were the ideal fit and offered a life away from the hustle and bustle of Istanbul.

He has his own security detail and is living in the nearby town of Yomra, where he now has a street named after him. He also employs a private chef and, unsurprisingly, continues to set standards in the gym and on the training ground.

By all accounts, Salah is thriving. He is a fan of Turkish coffee and is often spotted leaving the ground with Ayran - a traditional yogurt drink - but as much as he wants to explore the city, he knows of the difficulties given his reputation.

"Everyone wants to work with a star like Mohamed Salah," said Trabzonspor's Paul Onuachu, formerly of Southampton. "He adds so much and helps all of us and he contributes positively. I am grateful for him. It's a blessing to play with him."

Watching Salah in the flesh in a Conference League game against Freiburg, his pace has gone down a notch compared with his peak but the touch, quick feet and sheer quality is still there. And so is that knack of getting in goalscoring positions, even if his defensive duties - which were such a source of debate last season at Liverpool - are limited.

Salah believes he still has plenty to give for club and country, with aspirations to play in both the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations and 2030 World Cup, which will be partly held in North Africa.

No decision has been made about how long he will stay in Turkey, but there is growing belief among sources in the Middle East that he will move to Saudi Arabia when his two-year Trabzonspor deal expires in 2028. By then, he will be 36.

Salah signed a two-year deal with Trabzonspor in the summer of 2026

On initial thoughts, it is easy to question how and why Salah ended up here.

When he delivered that infamous mixed-zone interview at Leeds' Elland Road less than a year ago and the wheels of his departure from Liverpool were set in motion, surely no-one would have imagined his next destination would be this Turkish outpost near the Georgian border.

"I remember looking at him when we landed in Trabzon and seeing the crowds outside and how emotional it was," says Anil Dincer, one of the lawyers involved in Salah's move to Turkey.

"We already have Salah and Fabinho. So now we are waiting for [Virgil] Van Dijk," adds Serhat Sumer, a Trabzonspor fan.

Salah, of course, delivered so much joy to Liverpool and the intention here is the same. This is no drift towards retirement, but a player determined to prove he still belongs at the highest level and that football still has meaning beyond trophies and money.

Asked by BBC Sport if he had a message for Liverpool fans, Salah simply said "hello" and smiled. Given how rarely he spoke in the mixed zone during his time at Anfield, it is not in his nature to talk regularly on record.

Last season was Salah's least prolific at Anfield, but given Liverpool's struggles in front of goal in the Premier League, it is hard to argue they have replaced one of their greatest ever players.

Perhaps a time will come when the likes of Salah, Arne Slot and Richard Hughes will reveal more about the chain of events that led to the forward agreeing to terminate his contract a year early. As it is, none of them are at the club and that chapter is firmly closed.

Salah's influence that once helped shape the Premier League is now being felt on the shores of the Black Sea. He is Trabzonspor's force of nature. And the team known as the Black Sea Storm are rising and on the hunt for silverware with their Egyptian King.

A rock in the Trabzon highlands became a tourist destination after Salah's visit

#900. How Nick Cannon Really Feels About Mariah Carey Prenup

Ten years after Nick Cannon and Mariah Carey finalized their divorce, the  America’s Got Talent alum, who was married to the singer from 2008 to 2016, revealed the details of their prenup.

Boy, if you wanna know whether Nick Cannon and Mariah Carey had a prenup—he’ll tell you.

Ten years after the former couple—who share 15-year-old twins Moroccan and Monroe—finalized their divorce, the former America’s Got Talent host confirmed they “absolutely” signed a prenuptial agreement before tying the knot in 2008.

“Mariah Carey, her entity, her global conglomerate, is gonna make sure she is protected,” Cannon explained during a Nov. 9 appearance on the On Par with Maury Povich podcast. “Had no problem with it whatsoever. And when it was all said and done, I think it protected both of us.”

Although their divorce wasn’t finalized for two years following their 2014 breakup, the 46-year-old—dad to 10 additional children with five different women—said the process felt “easy.”

Nevertheless, it’s not a process Cannon sees himself going through again, as he doesn’t see himself ever getting remarried.

“I think because of some of the natures of, like, unmarrying are not good,” he continued. “And it’s just the process—you don’t realize it takes so long and how draining it is.”

And while divorce “didn’t affect” his friendship with Carey, he saw how divorce creates pressure points in relationships.

“It really could have affected how we handled one another as friends,” he admitted. “I saw the traps of how this could have turned really bad if we didn’t step in and really engage as a family.”

For Cannon, he considered the friendliness that exists between he and Carey an exception when it comes to divorce.

“We handled it so well,” he added. “We handled it out of love. Never heard me say a bad thing about her. Never heard her say a bad thing about me. And we just kind of made it about the kids.”

Meanwhile, Cannon—who is currently in a non-monogamous relationship with Bre Tiesi and Abby De La Rosa—previously went so far to admit that he and Carey might have another shot at romance in the future.

“We belong together,” he quipped to E! News in 2024, going on to say that he would “be stupid” not to get back together with Carey.

As for why the fantasy hasn’t turned into reality? Cannon acknowledged, “She don’t want me.”

For more on Cannon’s family tree, keep reading…

Children No. 1 and 2: Moroccan Cannon and Monroe Cannon

Mariah Carey gave birth to her and Nick's twins on April 30, 2011. The two announced their split in 2015 after six years of marriage and finalized their divorce a year later.

Beauty queen Brittany Bell gave birth to her and Nick's first child together, a boy, on Feb. 21, 2017.

Brittany and Nick welcomed their second baby together, a girl, in December 2020.

DJ Abby De La Rosa gave birth to her and Nick's twin boys on June 14, 2021.

Model Alyssa Scott welcomed a baby boy with Nick on June 23, 2021.

However, just five months after the arrival of their son, Nick shared the devastating news that Zen had passed away from brain cancer. "Alyssa was just the strongest woman I have ever seen," he said on the Dec. 7 episode of The Nick Cannon Show. "Never had an argument, never was angry. She was emotional when she needed to be but was always the best mom and continues to be the best mom possible. So I've got to say thank you to my entire family but specifically to Alyssa."

"You never know what someone is going through," he added. "Hug your family. Kiss somebody. Tell them you love them."

Model Bre Tiesi welcomed her first child with Nick on June 28, 2022. The baby boy weighed 8 pounds and 10 ounces at birth.

"I did it. An all natural unmedicated home birth," Bre shared in a July 2022 Instagram post. "This was the most humbling / limit pushing yet awakening and completely empowering experience. I can't thank my team enough for delivering my son safely."

Nick and model LaNisha Cole welcomed a daughter on Sept. 14, 2022.

Brittany gave birth to her third child with Nick on Sept. 23, 2022.

Abby gave birth to a baby girl, her third child with Nick, in November 2022.

Alyssa gave birth to her and Nick's daughter on Dec. 14, 2022.

The model shared an Instagram video showing the Wild 'n Out star helping to deliver their baby. "Our lives are forever changed," she wrote. "Zen is in every breath I take. I know his spirit was with us in the room that morning. I know he is watching down on us. He shows me signs everyday. I will hold onto this memory forever."

She continued, "I will remember the sound of Nicks voice saying 'it's a girl' and the look of everything we've been through flash across his face. I will remember the sound of her crying out with her first breath and feeling her heartbeat against mine. My sweet girl, I got my surprise!! We love you Halo Marie Cannon!"

#898. Who has made Troy's Premier League team of the week?

After every round of Premier League matches this season, BBC football pundit Troy Deeney will give you his team and manager of the week.

Here are this week's choices. Do you agree? Give us your thoughts using the comments form at the bottom of this page.

Bernd Leno (Fulham): Unbelievable couple of saves from him to keep Fulham in the game. I thought Newcastle should have been three or four up before Fulham got the equaliser.

Ronald Araujo (Liverpool): He is just the difference maker to that Liverpool backline. The injury-time Crystal Palace penalty that denied them a clean sheet was a terrible decision, but when he is in the team, they play better and look more solid.

Jair Cunha (Nottingham Forest): Exceptional. His goal helps, but exceptional at sniffing out the danger. Erling Haaland didn't have a sniff of a goal in Man City's defeat by Forest. Cunha will need to be really good going forward if they're the team Oliver Glasner wants.

Tarik Muharemovic (Leeds United): Many times he got caught one v one against Spurs but showed his ability to be chilled and calm under pressure and make his tackle. Very unassuming.

Nordi Mukiele (Sunderland): He was excellent again. He forced Chelsea to go wide and I think that was the key to them winning the game.

Leon Goretzka (Aston Villa): Although it was 4-4 in the end at Man Utd, Goretzka was a beast. He was calm under pressure and moved the ball really well as well. He obviously got a goal but his passing, movement and the ability to just be calm and handle every situation presented to him was really, really good.

Alexis Mac Allister (Liverpool): How this guy has not got a new deal I don't know. He keeps coming up big, high energy and he is vitally important to the way Liverpool play. When he is fit and available and firing on all cylinders it feels like they have a chance in this title race.

Enzo Le Fee (Sunderland): Where would Sunderland be without this guy? He has been good, he has been scoring, chipping in with big moments. Also his ability to take the ball when under pressure, take his side up the pitch and also have that little bit of innovative play and free thinking. He is exceptional.

Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall (Everton): Bossed the game for Everton against Coventry. Unbelievable goal but he absolutely bossed it. There was nothing more he could have done. Never gave the ball away, defensively he was solid. Attacking wise - goals and assists.

Thierno Barry (Everton): The two up front pick themselves, but probably the last time I would have them together in the same team. Did really well, two good goals against Coventry and probably should have had a third as well.

Liam Delap (Nottingham Forest): What a game for him and moment he needed. A lot of pressure from the outside, including myself. Hasn't shown up big this season but against his former team Man City, his former Chelsea manager Enzo Maresca as well, and he turned around and said, 'you know what, I am the man and you should have kept me around'. Scored two unbelievable goals, led the line well and looked physically fitter and stronger. Maybe now that confidence comes through and we see the best of him after the international break.

Mikel Arteta (Arsenal): I am going for Mikel Arteta simply because he has just won the Premier League. Well done. I said at the start of the season that, for me, Arsenal will win the league by 10 points and this weekend they did it. It's November and the season is officially over.

#897. How Kelly Clarkson Helps Daughter River Navigate "Hard" Junior High

The Voice’s Kelly Clarkson shared insight into parenting her daughter River Rose, 12, as she navigates school, friendships and conflict during an exclusive E! News interview: "Junior high sucks."

Kelly Clarkson's daughter is spreading her wings and learning to fly above the drama.

As her and late ex-husband Brandon Blackstock's 12-year-old daughter River Rose experiences the ups and downs of junior high school, the Voice coach shared how she took a chance, made a change and guided the tween to break away from the woes of adolescence.

"I'm a pretty progressive parent, so I'm like, 'No, no. You're gonna make your own mistakes, and that's OK,'" Clarkson told E! News' Will Marfuggi in an exclusive interview on The Voice season 30 live show red carpet on Nov. 9. "I'm not like an 'I told you so,' but I do implement advice."

"They're growing up," she continued. "One's in junior high, and junior high sucks. It's a hard age with friends, and arguing and stuff like that. I do offer advice, and I've had my daughter come back and be like, 'So you were right.'"

But the 44-year-old—also mom to 10-year-old son Remington Alexander with Blackstock—will always help her daughter stand a little taller, even when she doesn't heed her mom's warnings.

As she explained, "I've had them be like, 'OK, so I didn't do that, and I should have.'"

While Clarkson is hitting all the right notes of motherhood, she's also had a pitch-perfect time on The Voice alongside fellow coaches Adam Levine, Queen Latifah and Riley Green.

Although the Maroon 5 frontman took home gold last season with Alexia Jayy, he couldn't wait another minute to focus on this season.

"He doesn't really brag like that," Clarkson said. "He's not that guy. I totally would. I'd be like, 'Good luck,' just for fun or whatever. But he's pretty chill about it."

But the "Breakaway" singer would be lyin' if she said she wasn't looking forward to working with Latifah and Green as the newest additions experience the live rounds for the first time.

"What's amazing about Queen is she's such a legend," Clarson emphasized. "I know people throw around the term legend a lot, but she actually is. She's done so much, be it Broadway and movie musicals, be it rapping, be it singing, be it acting, whatever it is. She's just always doing stuff."

Simply put, "That brought just a legendary kind of status to the show for us this season."

Meanwhile, the "Worst Way" singer has definitely brought more than wine and roses to the singing competition.

"Riley is just currently crushing it on the charts, like everywhere," she continued. "His career is blown up. It's a different point in his career for him, too. So it's fun. They're bringing that different energy of what's happening in their world at this chapter in their lives."

While fans wait to see who wins big during The Voice season 30, press the red button and keep reading for surprising secrets about the series.

Does the winner of The Voice get any money?

The winner of The Voice is promised a recording contract with Universal Music Group, the monetary value of which is technically unknown.

But while NBC and series producers have never confirmed any amount, the last singer standing at the end of the competition reportedly gets $100,000.

Past winners have acknowledged getting paid, season 18 champ Todd Tilghman telling People in 2020, "I don't have any immediate plans to make any drastic changes tomorrow. I don't know for sure the direction my life will go in. There's a possibility that that money might pay the bills for a little while."

But, he added, since his wife had promised their kids a trip to Disney World, he guessed he'd be splurging on that too.

Not that the value of the music opportunities that open up for the winners should be discounted.

“I’ve got a catalog of songs. I have a lot of writer friends I want to collaborate with," season 27 winner Adam David of Team Bublé told Parade in May 2025. "The plan is to put out some music and go on to work. We’re going to put out some music, and we’re going to hit the road."

How does an aspiring contestant get to The Voice's Blind Auditions?

In addition to individual recruiting (such as when producers reached out to Frenchie Davis eight years after she was on American Idol), The Voice traditionally held in-person auditions around the U.S. Lately, however, the talent search is online, judges holding virtual open calls and weeding through video submissions to find singers who then may get a chance to sing for the coaches in hopes that at least one of them turns around.

Contestants must be at least 13 years old when they embark on their audition journey. The hopefuls have 90 seconds to introduce themselves and sing. They can sing anything they want but, per the show's FAQ page, they're encouraged to pick a tune "that best suits your voice and represents you as an artist."

Judges listen to auditions for "five or six days with approximately 18 to 20 auditions per day," executive producer Audrey Morrissey told SheKnows in 2018. Once they're selected for the blind round, she explained, "Artists are with us for several days prior to [their audition] to rehearse with our band, work with wardrobe/styling and camera block on the audition stage."

Then there's the filming to put together the packages introducing some of the hopefuls and their families, all of which came as a surprise to season six alum Ddendyl Hoyt. "I had no idea that reality TV was filmed kind of like a drama," she told the Washington Post in 2014, “So everything is filmed in segments and that’s kind of the longest process of it all.”

How many times can you audition for The Voice?

If at first you don't make it out of the untelevised rounds—or onto a team if you do make it to the blind auditions—you're free to try out as many times as you want, albeit only once per season.

"I can't be a mean judge," coach Reba McEntire, who won season 25 with Asher HaVon, told Newsweek in 2023. "It's good just to say, 'If you want to come back again, try it again next season, maybe a song that suits you, one that you're really comfortable with and that really shows your talent,' give them advice and encourage them to come back."

As of season 28, there's also the Carson Callback card to be played, in which longtime host Carson Daly grants an aspiring artist who didn't get any takers another shot.

Do The Voice contestants get to pick out their own clothing?

The show has a massive wardrobe department that ensures the contestants take the stage in elevated fashion—once they've made it onto a team.

"We shop for each artist to come up with great looks," Morrissey told SheKnows. "Once we get to the live shows, looks are customized for each specific performance."

How much time do the coaches really spend working with The Voice artists?

The celebrity coaches might not be pulling all-nighters, but they're invested in getting their teams ready for the battle rounds and beyond.

"The coaching sessions take place over four days," Morrissey said, "and the actual battle performances take two days."

Meanwhile, she added, how involved a coach gets with each artist "depends on the coach. Some love a big production and like working out all the details…Other coaches mainly focus on the music and arrangement for the performance."

Some coaches "are avid texters while others email," Morrissey added. "All off-camera interactions intensify as the artists move through the competition and the stakes get higher."

But it takes a village, former contestant Hoyt telling the Post, "What they don't show is all the coaching that comes from the staff: The vocal coaches, the band director, the producers, everyone has notes for you."

Snoop Dogg told Access Hollywood in September 2025, "The behind-the-scenes people don't get the credit that they deserve. It's a lot of people, moving things, making it happen…All of these people back here that make our job easy, all we gotta do is walk onstage and do what we do."

Who picks the songs the contestants sing on The Voice?

Between coaches and artists, Morrissey said, “The No. 1 communication is about song choice.”

The artists can theoretically offer their two cents when it comes to picking their songs, but usually the coaches rule on that front.

Season one's Frenchie—who competed under O.G. coach Christina Aguilera's tutelage—told Cosmopolitan in 2021 it was "always hysterical when the judges say, 'I don’t think that was a good song choice for you,' and I'm thinking, you picked that song.”

On the flip side, season 24 winner Huntley credited coach Niall Horan with helping him find his way, telling NBC Insider the One Direction alum "knows how to pick songs, I'll tell you that."

What sort of resources are available to help The Voice artists tend to their mental health?

Aspiring contestants are screened beforehand to see if they seem emotionally ready for the pressure that lies ahead, and then the show employs mental health professionals to help the artists both during and at the end of their journey.

“We had to start visiting to check on our well-being," season six alum Kat Perkins told Cosmopolitan of the counselors on staff. "The minute you are eliminated, you walk from that stage and into the psychiatrist’s office for a debriefing. They make sure that you talk about it. It’s very needed because you’ll never go through anything like it again. It’s traumatic and you’re not really emotionally set up to do something that big that quickly."

How do the chairs on The Voice really work?

The coaches are masters of their own domains, the big red chairs evolving over the years but always boasting the ability to turn around at the push of a button. In 2018 they received a sleek upgrade, including the addition of three more buttons—giving each coach the chance to block a fellow coach, once per round, from getting a chance at claiming the contestant behind the voice.

Not unlike a luxury car seat, in addition to an automobile-caliber aluminum frame and shiny paint job, each chair has self-adjusting heaters ("Me and Reba, we're the butt-warming kings," Snoop quipped to Access Hollywood) and dual cupholders (as requested by former coach Blake Shelton).

But, according to Perkins, the dramatic whoosh sound the chairs make when they turn around is added in post-production.

"You almost don’t notice it," she told Cosmo, "especially when you’re focusing and singing to the crowd that’s in the studio."

While congenial ribbing between coaches is part of the show's DNA, it was unclear at times over the course of the 16 seasons they were on The Voice together if Blake and Adam Levine were as exasperated with each other as they seemed.

"We are constantly at each other's throats, and sometimes we really do get mad at each other," Blake told The Tennessean in 2017. "We're those two guys you knew in high school where we have this bond that is unexplainable. It brings out the best and worst in both of us. It truly is an explosive relationship. And I know every trick to get under his skin."

Translation: "He's one of the best friends that I have, but I still want to kill him sometimes."

And even though they haven't competed against each other since 2019, Adam knows what the fans want.

"The Voice season 1 after party, at my house with dips--t @blakeshelton," the O.G. coach captioned a throwback pic ahead of his return to the show in February 2025 for season 27.

Meanwhile, subsequent crops of coaches were far less likely to tweet out each other's private phone numbers.

"You spend so much time together," Niall said during an NBC sit-down, "and I was hoping it wasn't going to be like this TV relationship where the cameras go around and we're like [feigning enthusiasm], 'Hey, Snoop Dogg!' I was always nervous about that, doing the show in the first place. I just didn't want it to be like a forced relationship, and it hasn't been that at all."

#896. Pochettino’s Manchester United interest is as natural as it is disruptive to the US

The former Tottenham manager is always going to be a subject of interest, but United’s job carries a rare power

As Mauricio Pochettino left the podium to close his final press conference of the last international window, he offered an ambiguous farewell.

“See you next …” Pochettino began as he headed to the tunnels of Allianz Field in Saint Paul, before cutting his sentence short. Then, a bit of a sing-song: “See you next, see you next.”

You don’t need an AI clanker’s autocomplete function to try closing the sentence. “See you next month” would have been synonymous with “see you next window”, after all. Still, the farewell felt poignant given questions about whether Pochettino was going to last a full four-year cycle as US men’s national team head coach.

In hindsight, maybe he had omitted adding something along the lines of: see you next, before I’m off to my next project.

From the moment that Pochettino and US Soccer announced his contract renewal in August, it was tough for many to imagine he would don his lavish safari shirts on the US sideline at the 2030 World Cup. This was Mauricio Pochettino, after all, a name brand in club management whose résumé teemed with unfinished business. Few great coaches hang their hat on being Premier League and Champions League runners-up.

Gone are the days where clubs with major financial considerations pull the plug on a whim. The time to strike is now at the start of an international window, when the next game isn’t for another couple of weeks. This serves as a crucial time to meet the squad, put them through their paces and hatch an initial scheme to stop the rot.

That puts international federations like US Soccer in an unenviable position. Pochettino is among the most eligible options for the Big Clubs, ensuring his continuing presence on managerial wishlists. And as long as that remains the case, the most likely window for advances from club suitors will be right in the stretch of time where a national team coach works hardest.

In September, that meant reheating years-old discourses about the apparent irresistibility of Tottenham Hotspur. Before the World Cup, Milan had come calling. And now, the focus turns to Old Trafford.

The attraction is logical. For over a decade, United have tested every managerial archetype possible since Sir Alex Ferguson called time on his illustrious career. Domestic options who punched above their weight class; chronic winners; onetime supernovas, with implosion all but inevitable; club legends; club custodians; young options ready for a Premier League closeup. Their tenures all ended the same.

Pochettino blends some of the best traits of Louis van Gaal and José Mourinho with a record of doing the work United hoped would happen under Ruben Amorim and Michael Carrick. His work building Tottenham into a threat on all fronts bolstered his culture-building cachet, showing his success at Espanyol and Southampton could scale. Even though his time at Paris Saint-Germain failed to yield their long-coveted Champions League title, he had experienced managing the egos of Neymar, Mbappé and Messi. Chelsea tested his tolerance for ownership-meddling. All of these factors inform Manchester United at present.

So no, the idea of Pochettino leaving the US so soon into his second term is hardly a shock. If it wasn’t to be United, or Tottenham, then he’d be a hot commodity if Real Madrid were to quickly abandon their reunion with Mourinho. If not them, then perhaps Milan again if their campaign were to sour before the festive season. And so on.

US Soccer deserves some credit for adequately preparing. For one thing, Pochettino’s retention was only made possible thanks to a billionaire super-donor, Ken Griffin. So while his wages dwarfed those of his predecessors, it hadn’t directly come at the expense of the federation’s other teams, initiatives or grassroots efforts.

The real boon is his release clause, a reported $10m (£7.5m) option that only a Big Club could afford to spring. Had Pochettino left after the World Cup, coach and federation would have parted with nothing more exchanged than a handshake and some pleasantries. Instead, they forged an insurance policy to make up for what could have been if Pochettino had stayed for a full cycle.

Of course, piles of money don’t qualify for World Cups. Should this international window be Pochettino’s last with the US, the onus will be on the federation to do what it couldn’t this summer and find an alternative to lead a program into an exciting new era. It would be a boon to the federation if that $10m pot was kept on standby to help foot the next coach’s wages, keeping the pool of possible candidates open and deep.

US Soccer will need to nail the next hire to reassure fans who fell for the team during their entertaining run at this year’s World Cup. That will probably be a project-by-committee, as the federation hasn’t seemed antsy to replace Matt Crocker after he quit his role as sporting director in April. And, if Pochettino was unlikely to be in the role all the way until 2030, perhaps it is a blessing that a split comes while the cycle is still dawning.

#895. What can you read into Premier League table after 10 games?

Only four teams have taken more points than Arsenal's 27 after 10 games

We are now more than a quarter of the way through the Premier League season, with each team having played 10 games.

History suggests the answer is quite a lot.

Last season, for instance, the top two - and two of the eventual bottom three - were in the exact spots at this stage that they in finished six months later.

How the Premier League table looks after 10 games

Arsenal are top of the table on 27 points - which is higher than the average number of points (23) champions have after 10 games.

In fact, only four teams have taken more points from their first 10 fixtures than the Gunners, and all four have gone on to win the league.

One small quirk that means Arenal fans should not start making plans for a parade just yet is that the only two previous sides to post exactly 27 points at this point of the campaign both failed to win the title - including the Gunners in 2022-23.

In 15 of the 34 Premier League seasons to date, the team top at this stage have gone on to win the title, so less than half the time.

While on 16 previous occasions, teams on 22 points, the tally of second-placed Brighton, or fewer after 10 games won the title, so there is still hope for the Seagulls.

However, the less good news for Fabian Hurzeler's side is that, bizarrely, the team in second after 10 games have won the title in just one of the past 18 seasons - that was Manchester City in 2022-23.

The fewest points any side has had at this stage and gone on to win the league is 18 - so City, on 21, and Liverpool, on 18, could still have a say.

Arsenal lead Brighton by five points, one fewer than the most points a team have ever come from behind at this stage to win a title.

Manchester United in 2002-03 and Manchester City in 2013-14 are the two to do that.

But Mikel Arteta and co can take comfort knowing the leaders at this stage have gone on to win the title in the past two seasons - after failing to do so in the previous four years.

Another 1-0 for relentless Arsenal - but did Odegaard spare VAR blushes?

Odegaard hits winner as Arsenal beat Hull to extend lead at top

Maresca's dream start turns into nightmare as title hopes hit

Crystal Palace are propping up the table having lost their past four league matches, but the stats suggest their position is far from terminal.

In total, 14 teams have stayed up having been bottom of the table at this point in the season - most recently Wolves in 2024-25.

Moreover, the fewest points a team has had after 10 games and stayed up at the end of the season is three.

That same Wolves team are the most recent of the four teams to have achieved that feat.

Sunderland, who climbed off the foot of the table with victory over Chelsea, had just four points at this stage in 2013-14 but still ended up finishing 14th.

Palace can also count themselves a little unfortunate to have amassed seven points and find themselves in 20th.

Only Bolton in 2002-03 have had more points (eight) after 10 games and been bottom - and that was in a situation when a number of other sides had played 11 matches.

Overall, 88 teams have previously had seven or fewer points after 10 Premier League games and 37 managed to stay up.

There is good news for Ipswich and Hull in that every promoted side since 2015-16 to take 11 points or more from their first 10 games - and there have been 14 of them - has survived.

The most recent promoted side to make as bright a start and go down were Cardiff in 2013-14, who were 12th with 12 points but finished bottom on 30 points.

The outlook is a little bleaker for Coventry.

Only two promoted sides in the past 11 seasons have taken fewer than 11 points and survived - Bournemouth in 2015-16 (eight) and Nottingham Forest in 2022-23 (five).

Frank Lampard's men are also the seventh promoted side to take exactly nine points from their first 10 games - two of the previous six survived (Wolves in 2009-10 and Leicester in 2014-15).

Lampard feels hair pull should have led to Coventry penalty

A long way to go then, still plenty of time for things to change. But how much do things really change from this point?

Well, not a great deal if we look at last season, when 15 of the 20 teams finished within three places of where they were after 10 games.

Aston Villa made the biggest jump, going from 11th at this stage to secure a top-four finish with time to spare.

So Champions League qualification remains well within grasp for Unai Emery's side, who are currently in 10th.

On the other extreme were Tottenham, riding high in sixth after 10 games before plummeting 11 places down the standings to finishing 17th, only securing survival on the final day.

As mentioned earlier, the top two and two of the eventual bottom three were already in their final positions by this point, while Burnley - the third relegated side - were only a place above the drop zone in 17th.

Perhaps Manchester United are in a relegation battle after all...?

#894. Keira Knightley Reveals Which of Her Movies She’s Only Seen Once

Keira Knightley—who played Juliet in the 2003 film Love Actually—revealed she’s only seen the Christmas classic one time: “I think I’m the person that knows it the least of anybody.”

If you look for it, you'll find that Keira Knightley’s love for Love Actually isn’t, actually, all around.

After all, the 41-year-old—who played Juliet in the 2003 rom-com—revealed she’s only seen the film once.

“I have not watched Love Actually since the premiere, which was when I was 18,” she told Heart in a video shared Nov. 9. “So, I think I’m the person that knows it the least of anybody.”

And before you go asking her what could be worse than the total agony of being in love, just know there’s a high chance she’ll have no idea what you’re on about.

“I know that people have a particular look on their face and then they say things to me and I know that means they’re quoting Love Actually,” she explained, “but I don’t really know what it is. It means nothing to me.”

Plus, it doesn’t help that the Pirates of the Caribbean actress’ time on set was so short.

“It was a week when I was 17,” she noted. “So, I don’t remember it, really.”

Even so, she’s proud of the film’s legacy.

“I quite like that it has this life,” she added. “Such a big life out there.”

The Richard Curtis-directed Christmas classic follows a slew of interconnected love stories in London during the weeks leading up to the Dec. 25 holiday. And while some characters in the film get the s--t kicked out of them by love, Knightley’s Juliet finds herself in a love triangle with her husband Peter (Chiwetel Ejiofor) and his best friend Mark (Andrew Lincoln).

The situation comes to a head when Mark shows up on Christmas to profess his love using cue-cards. And while the scene has cemented itself as one of the most unforgettable rom-com moments in history, the Pride & Prejudice star previously revealed she and the film’s director worked hard to make sure the grand gesture didn’t seem "stalker-ish" for viewers.

“My memory is of Richard, who is now a very dear friend, of me doing the scene, and him going, ‘No, you’re looking at [Andrew] like he’s creepy,’" she told Variety in 2024. "And I’m like, ‘But it is quite creepy.’"

That’s why Knightley changed up her facial expression to try to improve the scene, recalling that she continued by “having to redo it to fix my face to make him seem not creepy.”

For more proof that Love Actually secrets really are all around, read on…

1. Love Actually opens with scenes of travelers hugging and kissing their nearest and dearest as they reunite at London's Heathrow Airport."This is my favorite bit in the film, in fact," writer/director Richard Curtis said in a director's commentary version of the film. "This footage was shot by a hidden camera, which was in Heathrow Airport for a whole week."And the movie's team really had to jet to get permission to use these clips of real-life passengers."Every time they saw something they really liked, then the runner would charge off and ask the people to sign a bit of paper, whether or not they were happy that it should be shown in the film," he continued. "I still think it'll be quite a surprise to the people who go to the cinema and see themselves."As for the inspiration behind the scene, it came from Curtis' personal experience."I got stuck in an airport in L.A. for an hour and a half waiting for a package, and I just saw all these people just all hugging and kissing," he added. "And you realize that behind normal people in the park and in the street, there's all these stories of love."

2. The first character fans meet in the 2003 movie is Bill Nighy's Billy Mack. He's a rock and roll star approaching his golden years who releases a holiday cover of Wet Wet Wet's "Love Is All Around," which secured the No. 1 spot in the U.K. for 15 weeks after the release of Curtis' 1994 film Four Weddings and a Funeral.While it can be hard to imagine anyone but Nighy playing the part, he wasn't initially in the running for the role. It wasn't until the actor stepped in to help with a table read that Curtis knew he was the one for the job."I had two famous guys in mind to play the aging rocker Billy Mack, and I couldn't decide who to ask," the filmmaker told The Guardian in 2013. "But at the read-through, Bill did it so perfectly he became a definite yes. I've never told anyone else who I wanted. I'll put it in my will."

3. Martin Freeman has also shared his casting story. In Love Actually, he portrays a man named John who meets a woman named Judy (Joanna Page) while they're stand-ins for a movie and filming a sex scene. They have great conversations, go out on a date and fall in love.At the time of casting, Curtis had fallen in love with the U.K. version of The Office, which Freeman starred on from 2001 to 2003."I got attached to Love Actually because on the back of The Office Richard Curtis wrote me a very nice and flattering letter that contained a piece of chocolate in it," The Hobbit star recalled to Vanity Fair in 2020. "It was like a wrapped chocolate presented to me saying, 'I love The Office. I love what you did in The Office. It was amazing.'"

4. Before Thomas Brodie-Sangster was cast as Sam—a British boy who loses his mom and turns to his stepdad Daniel (Liam Neeson) to help him navigate his crush on American schoolmate Joanna—Joe Alwyn tried out for the part."This local community center where I took fencing lessons, this brilliant U.K. casting director called Shaheen Baig, she came around and she saw me there," The Favourite alum and ex of Taylor Swift, shared on a 2018 episode of Live With Kelly and Ryan. "It meant that I got time off school to go to this audition, so I went to it."In fact, Alwyn said he went through several rounds of auditions and "a whole series of workshops" before the filmmakers decided to go with Brodie-Sangster."I didn't get it in the end, obviously," he added, "but I do remember meeting Hugh Grant and Richard Curtis and sitting down and reading some scenes."

5. Colin Firth played Jamie, a writer who leaves London for his French country home after learning his girlfriend cheated on him with his brother. There, Jamie meets Portuguese housekeeper Aurélia (Lúcia Moniz). And while they don't speak the same language, they understand the feelings they've formed for each other.Jamie returns to England for a family Christmas party only to turn back around and, after learning some Portugese, propose to Aurélia. As he leaves, his niece yells, "I hate Uncle Jamie." And apparently, the name was a playful jab at Curtis' brother."Richard only called colin firth's character 'jamie' so the kids could say 'I hate uncle jamie,'" his wife and script writer Emma Freud tweeted in 2015. "His brother is called jamie."6. As for Aurélia, Curtis shared in the director's commentary the name was a nod to a friend-slash-employee who looked after his and Emma's son.7. In one scene, Jamie types outside while Aurélia clears a cup that had been holding down his papers, resulting in the wind sweeping them into a lake. Curtis said they used a wind machine so loud the lines were dubbed.Aurélia dives in to retrieve the pages, and Jamie follows. However, Curtis said the lake was only 18 inches deep at the time of filming."They're kneeling now, pretending to swim, but actually crawling along the bottom, the poor things," he added in the commentary. "And Colin got stung by a sort of animal and his elbow swelled up to the size of three avocados the next day."

8. Martine McCutcheon played Natalie. Her character joins the staff of the newly elected prime minster David (Grant), and the two develop a crush on each other.Curtis knew McCutcheon was the one for the role right from the get-go."I wrote Martine McCutcheon's part for her, too," he told The Guardian. "I even called the character Martine, though I had to change it before the read-through so she didn't think she'd already got it."

9. One of Grant's most famous scenes is when he does a celebratory dance to The Pointer Sisters' song "Jump (For My Love)" after standing up to the U.S. president. However, the actor wasn't thrilled about having to bust out some moves."I think I saw it in the script," Grant said in 2022 for The Laughter & Secrets of Love Actually: 20 Years Later – A Diane Sawyer Special, "and I thought, 'Well I'll hate doing that.'"In fact, Curtis said Grant "kept saying no." Still, the Notting Hill star gave in eventually."He was grumpy," Curtis added in the special. "It was a contractual obligation, a bit of contractual obligation acting."As for his reaction to Grant's performance in that scene?"I’m thinking, ‘Oh, good he’s doing it,'" he recalled. "Two, that’s agonizingly embarrassing.”And Grant admits he was off with his lip-synching and dancing."I'm out of rhythm by the way," he told Diane Sawyer, "especially at the beginning when I wiggle my ass.”However, Grant is willing to take a bow for the scene's ending."It was my idea to have the secretary lady catch me," he noted in the special. "Genius!"

10. While it's clear Laura Linney's character Sarah had a crush on her co-worker Karl (Rodrigo Santoro), it wasn't as obvious to viewers that the costars were navigating their own heartaches off-screen."Hands down, I got the best kiss. Sorry!" the actress said on a 2019 episode of The Graham Norton Show, referencing Sarah and Karl's make-out session that ends when she receives a call about her brother Michael's mental health battle and leaves to be with him. "And it was sweet because we were both very brokenhearted when we made that movie. He had just been dumped, I had just been dumped."Linney recalled how she and Santoro were "slumped in the van" lamenting about their breakups while on their way to film the scene."I turned to him, and I said, 'Well all day long we get to make each other feel better,'" she remembered, "and I think there is a sweetness to the scene because of that. We were both very sad."

11. Fans certainly said "I do" to the scene where Keira Knightley's charater Juliet marries Chiwetel Ejiofor's Peter, especially the part where the couple walks down the aisle and are surprised by musicians popping up from the church pews to perform The Beatles' "All You Need Is Love."While the wedding is a joyful part of the film, the inspiration for it actually came from a day of mourning: Jim Henson's funeral, which Curtis called "the most moving thing" he's ever attended."At the end of it, Frank Oz was talking and he suddenly lifted up Kermit's puppet and started to sing this song called 'One Voice,'" he explained in the director's commentary. "And it turned out all the guys in the memorial service had brought their puppets with them, and they lifted them up. And when you turned around and looked backwards, there were 50 puppets all singing. And Big Bird walked down the aisle of St. Paul's Cathedral, and they all came forward and just this massive chorus of puppets all singing. It was an extraordinary thing. So, this was our little stab at that."

12. After the wedding, Juliet visits Peter's best friend Mark (Andrew Lincoln) to see if he captured any video footage of the wedding day. While she was under the impression he hated her, she learns (after popping in a VHS tape featuring footage of only her at the wedding) that he's actually been shielding his romantic feelings for her. In the scene, Juliet wears a hat. However, Knightley explained there was a reason for this fashion choice.

“I got the biggest zit of my life when we were shooting this scene,” the actress told Jimmy Fallon on a 2019 episode of The Tonight Show. “And this scene is the important one, isn’t it? It was like another head growing out of my head."While Knightley said the makeup and lighting departments tried to hide the pimple, it was no use."There was nothing they could do," the Pride & Prejudice star added, "so the hat went on."

13. Fast-forward to later in the movie, Mark shows up at Juliet and Peter's house and rings the door bell. When she answers, he instructs her to tell her husband it's carol singers. Mark then comes clean about his love for her through a series of cards, including one that says "To me, you are perfect." In fact, Lincoln actually wrote out the cards himself.

"It is my handwriting!" The Walking Dead actor told Entertainment Weekly in 2013. "It’s funny, because the art department did it, and then I said, 'Well, can I do it?' because I like to think that my handwriting is really good. Actually, it ended up with me having to sort of trace over the art department’s, so it is my handwriting, but with a sort of pencil stencil underneath."Juliet and Mark then part ways after she gives him a controversial kiss goodbye. In a 2017 sequel short for Red Nose Day, it's revealed that Juliet and Peter are still married and that Mark has tied the knot with supermodel Kate Moss, who was featured on one of his cards in the OG film.

And that wasn't the only notable memory from shooting the romantic moment. Knightley also recalled having to redo her reaction to his cue card reveal a few times so that the gesture seemed less "stalker-ish."

In a December 2024 interview withVariety, she detailed changing up her facial expression to try to improve the scene, saying she wound up “having to redo it to fix my face to make him seem not creepy.”

14. While there appears to be a bigger age gap between Knightley and Brodie-Sangster in the movie, they're only five years apart IRL. She was 17 when they made the film, and he was 12.

15. Brodie-Sangster really did learn how to play the drums for Love Actually, in which his character picks up the instrument to impress his crush Joanna (Olivia Olson) at their school's Christmas concert."I did learn to play the drums for it,” he told The Sunday Post in 2017. “My dad’s a drummer and he taught me in my grandad’s basement bashing away on his old kit and trying to play along to 'All I Want For Christmas [Is You].'”16. And yes, that really was Olson singing the Mariah Carey hit."Everyone thinks she is lip-synching, and she was 9 or 10 years old," screenwriter Freud said at the Montclair Film Festival in 2016, per the event's recap of her presentation, "but that was her.”17. What's more, the scene where Joanna gives Sam a peck on the cheek at London's Heathrow Airport before she flies back to America marked her first on- and off-screen kiss.

"I was really nervous because I kind of had a crush on Thomas back in the day," the actress told E! News in 2016, "and I was also worried because I was taller than him."The kiss clearly left an impression on both characters. In the 2017 Red Nose Day special, it's revealed that Sam reconnected with Joanna in New York and that they got engaged—with them flying back to London to ask Neeson's character Daniel for his blessing.

18. Another unforgettable scene is when the character Harry (played by the late Alan Rickman) is trying to buy a necklace for his secretary Mia (Heike Makatsch) without his wife Karen (Emma Thompson) knowing, but the jewelry salesman Rufus (Rowan Atkinson) is moving at a snail's pace.And apparently, the Mr. Bean star was in no rush to finish filming the scene.

20. One of the most heartbreaking parts of the movie is when Karen finds the necklace in Harry's coat pocket, thinks it for her and then unwraps a Joni Mitchell CD for Christmas instead—leading her to realize he bought the necklace for another woman.After she puts on a smile for their children's Christmas concert, Karen tells Harry she knows what's going on. And while fans wondered if the couple remained married, Freud solved this mystery. "They stay together," she tweeted in 2015, "but home isn't as happy as it once was."And Freud says Harry's relationship with Mia went beyond the necklace."DEFINITELY had an affair," she wrote, "i begged richard just to make it a flirtation, but no. the whole way."

21. With several other beloved rom-coms under his belt—including Four Weddings and a Funeral, Notting Hill and Bridget Jones's Diary—Curtis resurfaced a scene he'd cut in a previous film for Love Actually.The scene stars a man named Colin (Kris Marshall), who is serving hors d'oeuvres at a wedding. In a failed attempt to flirt, he strikes up a conversation with a woman and tells her how bad the food is—except it turns out the woman is the caterer."This highly amusing scene coming up now about catering with this girl is a re-working of a highly amusing scene about catering, which bore remarkable resemblance down to the last line which was originally in Four Weddings and a Funeral," Grant, who appeared in both films, revealed while doing the director's commentary with Curtis, "which was one of my audition scenes, but which got cut from the final film."In fact, Curtis admitted he forgot to change the name from Charles in Four Weddings and a Funeral to Colin in Love Actually in a line of the re-worked script.22. Fed up with searching for love in the U.K., Colin decides to go to America and try his luck there. He flies to Wisconsin, where he meets a group of women at a bar, including one named Jeannie played by January Jones."January jones wrote half of her lines," Freud revealed in a tweet. "She was sooooo funny when we filmed that scene."

23. While there were several familiar faces in Love Actually, Freud revealed her and Curtis' kids also made a few cameos."THAT IS SCARLETT CURTIS THERE ON THE RIGHT," she tweeted about her daughter, who was dressed as one of the lobsters in the school's Nativity play (yes, you read that right). "NOT EVEN JOKING."In addition, she noted the boy with the crown and Spider-Man face-paint in the Christmas play is their son Jake, with her writing, "I gave birth to him."24. Looking back at the film two decades later, Curtis admits there are aspects of the film he wishes he could change."The lack of diversity makes me feel uncomfortable and a bit stupid," he admitted in the Diane Sawyer special. "I think there are three plots that have bosses and people who work for them."The director has also expressed regret over the film's comments about Natalie's weight.“I think I was behind, you know, behind the curve, and those jokes aren’t any longer funny," he told The Hollywood Reporter in 2023, "so I don’t feel I was malicious at the time, but I think I was unobservant and not as, you know, as clever as I should have been.”

25. While Love Actually features 10 different storylines, Curtis said he originally had more.

"At first, we had 14 different love stories, but the result was too long, so four ended up going, including two we'd actually shot," he told The Guardian. "One was based on a poster in Alan Rickman's office of two women in Africa. The camera actually went into the poster and heard them talking about their daughters' love lives. Another involved Emma Thompson's son getting into trouble at school and the camera following the harsh headmistress home."In the since-released deleted scenes, the headmistress can be seen heading home to take care of her partner Geraldine, who is dealing with an illness and later dies. Another deleted scene shows Sarah talking about family Christmas memories with her brother Michael. They ask each other how they're doing now. While Sarah says "everything's great," Michael gets real with her about his mental health struggles and says, "I'm in hell."Even though Curtis decreased the number of storylines, he admitted stringing the remaining ones together was no easy feat.

"Although all the strands come together in the airport at the end, it still felt like making 10 separate films," he told The Guardian. "It was a massively difficult edit. The order I originally wrote it in didn't work at all, so we had to reorder it completely. It was a bizarre four-month game of 3D chess."
